docs.title: Layer 1: MT4Account (Low-Level) — You are here!
docs.text: What: direct protobuf/gRPC communication with the MT4 terminal. Plain arguments in, protobuf *Data out; complete access to every MT4 function; highest control. Location: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_account.rb.

docs.title: Layer 2: MT4Service
docs.text: What: a friendly facade over MT4Account — plain arguments and typed Ruby Structs (Account, Quote, SymbolSpec…). No protobuf. Location: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_service.rb → overview.

docs.title: Layer 3: MT4Sugar
docs.text:
What: high-level convenience API — one-liners, risk-based position sizing, smart defaults. Location: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb → overview.

Each layer owns the one below it: MT4Sugar owns an MT4Service, which owns an MT4Account. From Sugar you can always reach down with sugar.service and sugar.account. (MetaRPC::MT4::Client aliases MT4Sugar; MetaRPC::MT4::Account aliases MT4Account.)

docs.title: 💡 Key concepts
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions. A server-side rejection raises MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError (carrying the mql error code); a transport failure raises the gRPC error. There are no error return values.
  • Session id is automatic. connect (ConnectEx) obtains a terminal session GUID; the SDK attaches it (+ your api key) to every later call and stream. Pass a stable id: per strategy so the gateway reuses one terminal.
  • MT4 has ORDERS, not positions. An open market order IS the position; its ticket is what you modify / close. Pending orders live in the same list, told apart by order_type (OO_OP_BUY/SELL = market, the ...LIMIT/STOP variants = pending). There are no separate "deals".
  • No trade retcode. Unlike MT5, MT4 has no returned_code: order_send returns OrderSendData with a ticket > 0 when the order is filled; a rejection raises ApiError (read e.mql_code: 130 invalid stops, 132 market closed, 134 not enough money, 138 requote). See Return Codes.

"Trade safe, code clean, and may your gRPC streams always flow smoothly."

docs.title: ✅ Getting an Account Summary
docs.text:
Request: full account summary (AccountSummaryData) from MT4. Fetch all core account metrics in a single call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#account_summary (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: AccountSummary (defined in mt4-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: AccountSummary(AccountSummaryRequest) → AccountSummaryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#account_summary(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A single RPC returning full account state: balance, equity, credit, currency, leverage, trade mode, margin / free margin / margin level / margin mode, and server time.
  • Why you need it. Fast dashboard / CLI status; double-check login / currency / leverage; connection heartbeat via server_time.
  • Sanity check. If account_login, account_currency, account_leverage, account_equity are set → the connection is alive.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it to display real-time account state and sanity-check connectivity:

  • Dashboard / CLI status in one call.
  • Verify balance & equity before trading.
  • Terminal heartbeat via server_time / server_time_utc and server_utc_offset_seconds.

Prefer plain values? MT4Service#account_info returns a friendly Account Struct (named fields, times as numbers) instead of protobuf.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Retrieves full account information in a single call.
  # Returns the raw AccountSummaryData (read fields with snake_case accessors);
  # raises ApiError on failure.
  def account_summary -> Mt4TermApi::AccountSummaryData
end

Request message:

AccountSummaryRequest {} (empty message — the SDK builds it for you; account_summary takes no arguments)

Reply message:

AccountSummaryReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountSummaryData data = 1;
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

MT4Account unwraps the oneof: it returns data on success and raises ApiError (carrying the server-side Error) otherwise.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
No parameters. account_summary takes no arguments — the SDK sends an empty AccountSummaryRequest.

There is no per-call timeout argument. Each call runs on the account's deadline (timeout, default 60 s). Tune it on the account:

acct.timeout = 15   # seconds — deadline for ordinary read RPCs

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountSummaryData
docs.text:
Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description account_login account_login Integer Trading account login (ID). account_balance account_balance Float Balance excluding floating P/L. account_equity account_equity Float Equity = balance + credit + floating P/L. account_user_name account_user_name String Account holder name. account_leverage account_leverage Integer Leverage (e.g. 100 for 1:100). account_trade_mode account_trade_mode Symbol Demo / Contest / Real — see enum below. account_company_name account_company_name String Broker / company display name. account_currency account_currency String Deposit currency (e.g. "USD"). server_time server_time Timestamp Server time at response (broker time zone). .seconds → unix seconds. server_time_utc server_time_utc Timestamp The same moment in UTC. account_credit account_credit Float Credit amount (bonus funds). is_investor is_investor Boolean Connected with the investor (read-only) password. utc_server_time_shift_minutes utc_server_time_shift_minutes Integer Server offset from UTC (minutes). server_utc_offset_seconds server_utc_offset_seconds Integer Broker offset from UTC in seconds (positive = ahead). account_margin account_margin Float Margin currently used by open orders. account_margin_free account_margin_free Float Free margin available for new orders. account_margin_level account_margin_level Float Margin level in percent (equity / margin × 100); 0 when no margin is used. account_margin_mode account_margin_mode Symbol Margin mode — see enum below. account_trade_allowed account_trade_allowed Boolean Trading allowed for this account. account_trade_expert account_trade_expert Boolean Automated (EA) trading allowed.

🧮 Floating profit: the summary has no dedicated profit field — compute account_equity - account_balance - account_credit (MT4: Equity = Balance + Credit + Floating P/L).

docs.title: 🧱 Related enums (from proto)
docs.text: 💡 Enum usage note: generated protobuf enums come back as Ruby symbols. Compare against the full constant, e.g. s.account_trade_mode == :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO.

docs.title: EnumAccountTradeMode
docs.text:
enum EnumAccountTradeMode {
  ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO    = 0;  // demo / practice
  ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST = 1;  // contest
  ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL    = 2;  // real trading
}

def trade_mode_to_s(mode)
  case mode
  when :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO    then "DEMO"
  when :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST then "CONTEST"
  when :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL    then "REAL"
  else "UNKNOWN(#{mode})"
  end
end

docs.title: EnumAccountMarginMode
docs.text:
enum EnumAccountMarginMode {
  ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_NETTING = 0;  // netting (one position per symbol)
  ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_EXCHANGE       = 1;  // exchange margin
  ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING = 2;  // hedging (many orders per symbol) — typical MT4
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: a server-side rejection raises MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError; a transport failure raises the gRPC error. Wrap in begin/rescue.
  • Default timeout: read RPCs use the account's timeout (default 60 s).
  • Timestamps: server_time / server_time_utc are google.protobuf.Timestamp; read .seconds for unix seconds, or use the friendly MT4Service#account_info which returns numbers.
  • Session is automatic: connect obtains the terminal id and the SDK attaches it to this call — you never pass it yourself.
  • No single-property getter on MT4: there is no account_info_double/integer/string (that is MT5). Read the field you need off the summary.

docs.title: 1) Basic usage
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

acct = MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account.new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443, api_key: ENV["MRPC_API_KEY"])
acct.connect(1235959737, "password", server: "EGlobal-Demo")

s = acct.account_summary
puts "Account Login: #{s.account_login}"
puts "Balance: #{s.account_balance.round(2)} #{s.account_currency}"
puts "Equity: #{s.account_equity.round(2)}"
puts "Leverage: 1:#{s.account_leverage}"

docs.title: 2) Compact status line for a CLI
docs.text:
def print_account_status(acct)
  s = acct.account_summary
  puts "Acc #{s.account_login} | #{s.account_currency} | " \
       "Bal #{s.account_balance.round(2)} | Eq #{s.account_equity.round(2)} | " \
       "Lev 1:#{s.account_leverage} | Mode #{trade_mode_to_s(s.account_trade_mode)}"
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError => e
  puts "❌ Error: #{e.message}"
end
# Output: Acc 1235959737 | USD | Bal 10000.0 | Eq 10050.25 | Lev 1:100 | Mode DEMO

docs.title: 3) Floating profit & margin health
docs.text:
def print_health(acct)
  s = acct.account_summary
  floating = s.account_equity - s.account_balance - s.account_credit
  level = s.account_margin_level                    # 0 when flat

  puts "Floating P/L: #{floating.round(2)}"
  if level.zero?       then puts "No open margin"
  elsif level < 100    then puts "⚠️ Margin level critical!"
  elsif level < 200    then puts "⚠️ Low margin level"
  else                      puts "✅ Healthy margin level"
  end
end

docs.title: 4) Server time with timezone shift
docs.text:
def print_server_time(acct)
  s = acct.account_summary
  utc    = Time.at(s.server_time_utc.seconds).utc
  broker = Time.at(s.server_time.seconds).utc
  puts "Server time (UTC): #{utc.iso8601}"
  puts "Server time (broker): #{broker.iso8601}"
  puts "Broker offset from UTC: #{s.server_utc_offset_seconds} seconds"
end

docs.title: 5) Structured data model
docs.text:
AccountView = Struct.new(:login, :currency, :balance, :equity, :floating, :leverage, :trade_mode, :company, keyword_init: true)

def from_proto(s)
  AccountView.new(
    login: s.account_login, currency: s.account_currency,
    balance: s.account_balance, equity: s.account_equity,
    floating: s.account_equity - s.account_balance - s.account_credit,
    leverage: s.account_leverage, trade_mode: trade_mode_to_s(s.account_trade_mode),
    company: s.account_company_name
  )
end

p from_proto(acct.account_summary)

docs.title: 6) Error handling
docs.text:
def try_get_summary(acct)
  acct.account_summary
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError, GRPC::BadStatus => e
  puts "Failed to get account summary: #{e.message}"
  nil
end

docs.title: Health check
docs.text:
def account_healthy?(acct)
  s = acct.account_summary
  s.account_login.positive? && !s.account_currency.empty? && s.account_leverage.positive?
rescue StandardError
  false
end

docs.title: Monitor account changes
docs.text:
def monitor_account(acct, interval_s)
  loop do
    s = acct.account_summary
    puts "[#{Time.now.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] Balance: #{s.account_balance.round(2)} | Equity: #{s.account_equity.round(2)}"
    sleep interval_s
  rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError => e
    puts "❌ Error: #{e.message}"
  end
end
# Usage: monitor_account(acct, 5)

  • ServerTimezone — broker UTC offset for interpreting *_utc timestamps.

docs.title: MT4Account · Account Information — Overview
docs.text:
The account's money picture and trading statistics: a one-call snapshot, aggregated stats, the equity curve, and per-order unrealized-P/L extrema.

These methods are read-only. account_summary lives on mt4_term_api.AccountHelper; the four statistics methods on mt4_term_api.TradeStats. Each returns the raw *Data (read fields with snake_case accessors), or raises ApiError.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• AccountSummary — all account info at once (login, balance, equity, credit, leverage, currency, margin / free margin / margin level / margin mode, server time). Returns the EnumAccountTradeMode and EnumAccountMarginMode enums.
  • TradeStats — aggregated trade statistics (drawdowns, profit factor, Sharpe ratio, expectancy, win/loss split, trades, growth %). Returns StatsData.
  • TradeStatsEquityHistory — the stats plus equity/balance chart points and per-trade series. Returns StatsWithChartsData.
  • EquityHistory — just the equity-curve points (balance, equity, drawdowns, realized/unrealized P/L). Returns [EquityPointData].
  • TradeUnrealizedPL — the max / min unrealized P/L reached per open order. Returns [TradeUnrealizedExtremaData].

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• account_summary → the one-stop shop for a complete snapshot. One RPC, everything for a dashboard, a pre-trade affordability check, or a connection heartbeat. MT4 (unlike MT5) does return account_margin, account_margin_free, account_margin_level here.
  • trade_stats → a performance report: win rate, drawdown, profit factor, Sharpe, expectancy — computed over your history since a start time.
  • trade_stats_equity_history → the same stats and the equity/balance curve in one call.
  • equity_history → just the curve — points you can plot.
  • trade_unrealized_pl → how far each open trade swung (best/worst unrealized P/L and when).

Rule of thumb: need the account state → account_summary; need performance → trade_stats; need a chart → equity_history.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Enums used Complete account snapshot (all values) account_summary AccountSummaryData Output: EnumAccountTradeMode, EnumAccountMarginMode Performance report trade_stats StatsData — Stats + equity/balance charts trade_stats_equity_history StatsWithChartsData — Equity-curve points only equity_history [EquityPointData] — Per-order unrealized-P/L extrema trade_unrealized_pl [TradeUnrealizedExtremaData] —

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Margin is in the summary — account_summary already returns account_margin, account_margin_free, account_margin_level and account_margin_mode. MT4 has no AccountInfoDouble RPC (that is MT5), so there is no single-property getter — read the field off the summary.
  • Floating profit — the summary carries no dedicated profit field; compute account_equity − account_balance − account_credit (MT4: Equity = Balance + Credit + Floating).
  • Stats window bound is a STRING — the four statistics requests take an optional from (broker time, yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss) or from_utc (UTC ISO-8601) — send one, not both; omit for the full account history. The SDK converts a Ruby Time to the ISO string for you.
  • Timeouts — stats run on a longer deadline (120 s) because they scan history; simple reads use the account's timeout (default 60 s).

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
# Complete account snapshot
s = acct.account_summary
puts "Balance: #{s.account_balance.round(2)}, Equity: #{s.account_equity.round(2)}, Leverage: 1:#{s.account_leverage}"

# Performance stats for the last 30 days
st = acct.trade_stats(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
puts "Trades: #{st.trades}  Profit factor: #{st.profit_factor.round(2)}  Total P/L: #{st.summary.total_profit.round(2)}"

# Equity curve points
pts = acct.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
puts "#{pts.size} points, last equity #{pts.last&.equity}"

# How far each open trade swung
acct.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 24 * 3600).each do |x|
  puts "##{x.ticket} #{x.symbol}: max +#{x.max_unrealized_pl.round(2)} / min #{x.min_unrealized_pl.round(2)}"
end

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used in Account Information
docs.text:
Only account_summary carries enums — the statistics methods return plain numeric fields.

Method Output enum Accessor Values account_summary EnumAccountTradeMode account_trade_mode :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO (0) · :..._CONTEST (1) · :..._REAL (2) account_summary EnumAccountMarginMode account_margin_mode :ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_NETTING (0) · :..._EXCHANGE (1) · :..._RETAIL_HEDGING (2) 
s = acct.account_summary
case s.account_trade_mode
when :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO then puts "Demo account"
when :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL then puts "Real account"
end

docs.title: 💹 Equity Curve Points
docs.text:
Request: just the equity / balance curve ([EquityPointData]) over a window — the points you plot.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#equity_history (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Proto definition: EquityHistory

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Method: EquityHistory(EquityHistoryRequest) → EquityHistoryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::TradeStats::Stub#equity_history(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The equity-curve points only — no aggregate stats.
  • Why you need it. Plot an equity / balance chart; feed a drawdown or risk visual.
  • Returns an array. The SDK unwraps the reply and returns data.points as a ready array.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Equity / balance curve points since `from_utc` (or broker-local `from`).
  # `exclude_same_bars` drops consecutive flat points. Returns [EquityPointData].
  def equity_history(from_utc: nil, from: nil, exclude_same_bars: false) -> Array<Mt4TermApi::EquityPointData>
end

Request message:

EquityHistoryRequest {
  string from              = 1;  // broker server time, "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss"
  string from_utc          = 2;  // UTC ISO-8601
  bool   exclude_same_bars = 3;  // drop flat/duplicate points
}

Reply message: EquityHistoryReply { oneof response { EquityHistoryData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — EquityHistoryData { repeated EquityPointData points = 1; }. The SDK returns points as an array.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Description from_utc Time / String / nil nil Window start in UTC (converted to ISO-8601 for you). from Time / String / nil nil Window start in broker server time. Use instead of from_utc. exclude_same_bars Boolean false Skip consecutive points with no change.

Runs on a 120 s deadline.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [EquityPointData]
docs.text:
Each point:

Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description time time Timestamp Point time (broker time zone). .seconds → unix. time_utc time_utc Timestamp The same moment in UTC. balance balance Float Account balance at this point. equity equity Float Account equity at this point. balance_drawdown_raw balance_drawdown_raw Float Balance drawdown (money). balance_drawdown_relative balance_drawdown_relative Float Balance drawdown (fraction). equity_drawdown_raw equity_drawdown_raw Float Equity drawdown (money). equity_drawdown_relative equity_drawdown_relative Float Equity drawdown (fraction). realized_pl realized_pl Float Realized P/L up to this point. unrealized_pl unrealized_pl Float Open-trade P/L at this point. cash_flow cash_flow Float Deposits / withdrawals at this point.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One window bound — from_utc or from; omit for full history.
  • exclude_same_bars: true for long windows → fewer, more meaningful points.
  • Timestamps are Timestamp — read .seconds, or convert with server_timezone.
  • Need the numbers too? trade_stats_equity_history returns stats + charts together.

docs.title: 1) Last balance & equity
docs.text:
pts = acct.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
last = pts.last
puts "#{pts.size} points, equity #{last&.equity&.round(2)} balance #{last&.balance&.round(2)}"

docs.title: 2) Max relative equity drawdown on the curve
docs.text:
pts = acct.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600, exclude_same_bars: true)
worst = pts.map(&:equity_drawdown_relative).max || 0.0
puts "Max equity drawdown on curve: #{(worst * 100).round(1)}%"

docs.title: 3) Export CSV
docs.text:
require "csv"
CSV.open("equity.csv", "w") do |csv|
  csv << %w[time_utc balance equity]
  acct.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600).each do |p|
    csv << [Time.at(p.time_utc.seconds).utc.iso8601, p.balance, p.equity]
  end
end

  • TradeStatsEquityHistory — stats + charts in one call.
  • TradeUnrealizedPL — per-order unrealized-P/L extrema.

docs.title: 📊 Aggregated Trade Statistics
docs.text:
Request: a full performance report (StatsData) computed over your trading history since a start time — drawdowns, profit factor, Sharpe ratio, expectancy, win/loss split and more.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#trade_stats (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Proto definition: TradeStats (defined in mt4-term-api-trade-stats.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Method: TradeStats(TradeStatsRequest) → TradeStatsReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::TradeStats::Stub#trade_stats(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that scans your closed-trade history and returns dozens of aggregate metrics.
  • Why you need it. Performance reports, strategy scorecards, risk dashboards — without pulling every deal yourself.
  • Window. Pass a start time (from_utc or broker-local from); omit it for the whole account history.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Aggregated trading statistics since `from_utc` (or broker-local `from`).
  # Returns the raw StatsData; raises ApiError on failure.
  def trade_stats(from_utc: nil, from: nil) -> Mt4TermApi::StatsData
end

Request message:

TradeStatsRequest {
  string from     = 1;  // broker server time, "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss"
  string from_utc = 2;  // UTC ISO-8601
}

⚠️ The window bound is a STRING, not a Timestamp. Send one of from / from_utc, or neither for full history. The SDK converts a Ruby Time to the ISO string for you — trade_stats(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).

Reply message: TradeStatsReply { oneof response { StatsData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Description from_utc Time / String / Integer / nil nil Window start in UTC. A Time/epoch is converted to ISO-8601 for you. from Time / String / nil nil Window start in broker server time (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss). Use instead of from_utc, not both.

Runs on a 120 s deadline (it scans history).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — StatsData
docs.text:
Headline scalars:

Field Type Description trades Integer Number of closed trades counted. profit_factor Float Gross profit ÷ gross loss (> 1 = profitable). sharpe_ratio Float Risk-adjusted return. standard_deviation Float Dispersion of trade results. ghpr Float Geometric holding-period return. growth_percent Float Account growth over the window, %. pips Float Net pips. lots Float Total volume traded, lots. comissions Float Total commissions (proto spelling: comissions). deposits / withdrawals Float Cash in / out over the window. average_trade_length String Mean holding time (human-readable). max_balance_drawdown_raw / _relative Float Deepest balance drawdown (money / fraction). max_equity_drawdown_raw / _relative Float Deepest equity drawdown (money / fraction).

Nested messages (each carries a value plus context):

Field Message What it holds summary TradeSummaryData open_trades, open_profit, day_profit, week_profit, month_profit, total_profit. profitability ProfitabilityData won_trades, won_trades_percent, lost_trades, lost_trades_percent. average_win / average_lost money value Mean win / loss. longs_won / shorts_won won/total split Long- vs short-side win rate. best_trade / worst_trade money value Largest single win / loss. best_trade_pips / worst_trade_pips pip value Best / worst in pips. z_score / expectancy value Streak significance / expected value per trade. markets […] (repeated) Per-symbol breakdown.

Explore the exact nested fields offline with the Protobuf Inspector: ruby examples/demos/helpers/17_protobuf_inspector.rb StatsData.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One window bound. Pass from_utc or from, never both.
  • Proto spelling. The commission field is comissions (single "m") — a server-side spelling, kept as-is.
  • Empty history. With no trades in the window, counts are 0 and ratios may be 0 / NaN-like — guard before dividing.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue for MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError.

docs.title: 1) Basic report
docs.text:
st = acct.trade_stats(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
puts "Trades: #{st.trades}"
puts "Profit factor: #{st.profit_factor.round(2)}"
puts "Sharpe: #{st.sharpe_ratio.round(2)}"
puts "Total P/L: #{st.summary.total_profit.round(2)}"

docs.title: 2) Win/loss split
docs.text:
p = acct.trade_stats(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600).profitability
puts "Won #{p.won_trades} (#{p.won_trades_percent.round(1)}%) / Lost #{p.lost_trades} (#{p.lost_trades_percent.round(1)}%)"

docs.title: 3) Drawdown guard
docs.text:
st = acct.trade_stats   # full history
if st.max_equity_drawdown_relative > 0.3
  puts "⚠️ Equity drawdown exceeded 30% at some point"
end

docs.title: 4) Scorecard line
docs.text:
st = acct.trade_stats(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 90 * 24 * 3600)
puts format("90d | %d trades | PF %.2f | growth %.1f%% | maxDD %.1f%%",
            st.trades, st.profit_factor, st.growth_percent, st.max_equity_drawdown_relative * 100)

docs.title: 5) Error handling
docs.text:
def safe_stats(acct, **win)
  acct.trade_stats(**win)
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError, GRPC::BadStatus => e
  warn "stats failed: #{e.message}"
  nil
end

docs.title: 📉 Unrealized-P/L Extrema
docs.text:
Request: the maximum and minimum unrealized P/L each open order reached over a window ([TradeUnrealizedExtremaData]) — how far every trade swung before you were in it.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#trade_unrealized_pl (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Proto definition: TradeUnrealizedPL

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats

  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::TradeStats::Stub#trade_unrealized_pl(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Per-order max / min floating P/L and the time each extreme happened.
  • Why you need it. Measure MFE/MAE (maximum favorable / adverse excursion) — did your stop sit too tight, your target too far?
  • Returns an array. The SDK returns data.extrema as a ready array.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Unrealized-P/L extrema per open order since `from_utc` (or broker-local `from`).
  # Returns [TradeUnrealizedExtremaData].
  def trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: nil, from: nil) -> Array<Mt4TermApi::TradeUnrealizedExtremaData>
end

Request message:

TradeUnrealizedPLRequest {
  string from     = 1;  // broker server time, "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss"
  string from_utc = 2;  // UTC ISO-8601
}

Reply message: TradeUnrealizedPLReply { oneof response { TradeUnrealizedPLData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — TradeUnrealizedPLData { repeated TradeUnrealizedExtremaData extrema = 1; }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Description from_utc Time / String / nil nil Window start in UTC (converted to ISO-8601 for you). from Time / String / nil nil Window start in broker server time. Use instead of from_utc.

Runs on a 120 s deadline.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [TradeUnrealizedExtremaData]
docs.text:
Each entry:

Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description ticket ticket Integer Order ticket. symbol symbol String Instrument. max_unrealized_pl max_unrealized_pl Float Best floating P/L reached (MFE). max_unrealized_time max_unrealized_time Timestamp When the max was reached (broker time). max_unrealized_time_utc max_unrealized_time_utc Timestamp The same moment in UTC. min_unrealized_pl min_unrealized_pl Float Worst floating P/L reached (MAE). min_unrealized_time min_unrealized_time Timestamp When the min was reached (broker time). min_unrealized_time_utc min_unrealized_time_utc Timestamp The same moment in UTC.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One window bound — from_utc or from; omit for full history.
  • MFE/MAE analysis — compare max_unrealized_pl against each trade's realized result to spot targets left on the table, and min_unrealized_pl to spot stops nearly hit.
  • Timestamps are Timestamp — read .seconds.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) List extrema per order
docs.text:
acct.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 24 * 3600).each do |x|
  puts format("#%d %-8s  MFE +%.2f  MAE %.2f", x.ticket, x.symbol, x.max_unrealized_pl, x.min_unrealized_pl)
end

docs.title: 2) Worst adverse excursion
docs.text:
rows = acct.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
worst = rows.min_by(&:min_unrealized_pl)
puts "Deepest drawdown: ##{worst&.ticket} #{worst&.symbol} #{worst&.min_unrealized_pl&.round(2)}" if worst

docs.title: 3) Time-to-peak
docs.text:
acct.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).each do |x|
  t = Time.at(x.max_unrealized_time_utc.seconds).utc
  puts "##{x.ticket} peaked at #{t.strftime('%H:%M')} (+#{x.max_unrealized_pl.round(2)})"
end

docs.title: 📋 Listing Open Orders
docs.text:
Request: every open order (market and pending) in full detail ([OpenedOrderInfo]). On MT4 an open market order is the position.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#opened_orders (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: OpenedOrders

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: OpenedOrders(OpenedOrdersRequest) → OpenedOrdersReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#opened_orders(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The current book of open orders — market positions and working pendings together.
  • Why you need it. Manage trades: read P/L, SL/TP, volume, magic; find a ticket to modify or close.
  • Returns an array. The SDK unwraps the reply and returns data.order_infos as a ready array.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # All open orders (market + pending), sorted by `sort`.
  # Returns [OpenedOrderInfo]; raises ApiError on failure.
  def opened_orders(sort: :SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC) -> Array<Mt4TermApi::OpenedOrderInfo>
end

Request message:

OpenedOrdersRequest {
  EnumOpenedOrderSortType sort_type = 1;
}

Reply message: OpenedOrdersReply { oneof response { OpenedOrdersData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — OpenedOrdersData { repeated OpenedOrderInfo order_infos = 1; }. The SDK returns order_infos as an array.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description sort Symbol (EnumOpenedOrderSortType) :SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC Server-side ordering of the result.

docs.title: EnumOpenedOrderSortType
docs.text:
enum EnumOpenedOrderSortType {
  SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC       = 0;
  SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC      = 1;
  SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC = 2;
  SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC = 3;
}

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [OpenedOrderInfo]
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description ticket ticket Integer Order ticket (the id you modify / close). symbol symbol String Instrument. order_type order_type Symbol OpenedOrderType — market (OO_OP_BUY/SELL) or pending — see enum below. lots lots Float Volume in lots. open_price open_price Float Entry price (for pendings, the order price). stop_loss stop_loss Float SL price (0 = none). take_profit take_profit Float TP price (0 = none). profit profit Float Current floating P/L (account currency). swap swap Float Accrued swap. commision commision Float Commission (proto spelling: single "m"). magic_number magic_number Integer EA magic number (your strategy tag). comment comment String Order comment. open_time open_time Timestamp Open time (broker time zone). open_time_utc open_time_utc Timestamp Open time in UTC. expiration_time expiration_time Timestamp Pending-order expiry (broker time). expiration_time_utc expiration_time_utc Timestamp Pending-order expiry (UTC). position_index position_index Integer Internal index. sort_index sort_index Integer Index under the chosen sort. account_login account_login Integer Owning account login.

docs.title: OpenedOrderType
docs.text:
enum OpenedOrderType {
  OO_OP_BUY       = 0;  // market  — this IS a position
  OO_OP_SELL      = 1;  // market  — this IS a position
  OO_OP_BUYLIMIT  = 2;  // pending
  OO_OP_SELLLIMIT = 3;  // pending
  OO_OP_BUYSTOP   = 4;  // pending
  OO_OP_SELLSTOP  = 5;  // pending
  OO_OP_BALANCE   = 6;  // non-trade book entry
  OO_OP_CREDIT    = 7;  // non-trade book entry
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Market vs pending. OO_OP_BUY/SELL are your open positions; the ...LIMIT/STOP types are pending. OO_OP_BALANCE/CREDIT are ledger entries, not trades.
  • Filter in Ruby. There is no server-side magic/symbol filter — select client-side (or use MT4Service#positions).
  • 0 SL/TP means none — not price zero.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) List everything
docs.text:
acct.opened_orders.each do |o|
  puts format("#%d %-8s %-12s lots %.2f  P/L %.2f", o.ticket, o.symbol, o.order_type, o.lots, o.profit)
end

docs.title: 2) Positions only (market orders)
docs.text:
MARKET = %i[OO_OP_BUY OO_OP_SELL]
positions = acct.opened_orders.select { |o| MARKET.include?(o.order_type) }
puts "open positions: #{positions.size}, floating #{positions.sum(&:profit).round(2)}"

docs.title: 3) Pending orders for one symbol
docs.text:
pending = acct.opened_orders.reject { |o| %i[OO_OP_BUY OO_OP_SELL OO_OP_BALANCE OO_OP_CREDIT].include?(o.order_type) }
pending.select { |o| o.symbol == "EURUSD" }.each { |o| puts "##{o.ticket} #{o.order_type} @ #{o.open_price}" }

docs.title: 4) Find a ticket by magic
docs.text:
mine = acct.opened_orders.find { |o| o.magic_number == 600_101 }
puts mine ? "found ##{mine.ticket}" : "none"

docs.title: 5) Error handling
docs.text:
def safe_open_orders(acct)
  acct.opened_orders
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError, GRPC::BadStatus => e
  warn "opened_orders failed: #{e.message}"
  []
end

docs.title: 🎟️ Open Order Tickets
docs.text:
Request: just the ticket numbers of the open orders ([Integer]) — the lightweight way to poll "what's open".

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#opened_orders_tickets (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: OpenedOrdersTickets

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: OpenedOrdersTickets(OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) → OpenedOrdersTicketsReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#opened_orders_tickets(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Only the ticket ids of currently open orders — no detail payload.
  • Why you need it. Cheap, frequent polling: detect when an order opens/closes without pulling full records; diff against a previous snapshot.
  • Returns an array of integers. The SDK returns data.tickets as a ready array.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Only the tickets of the open orders. Returns [Integer]; raises ApiError on failure.
  def opened_orders_tickets -> Array<Integer>
end

Request message:

OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {} (empty — the SDK builds it; takes no arguments)

Reply message: OpenedOrdersTicketsReply { oneof response { OpenedOrdersTicketsData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — OpenedOrdersTicketsData { repeated int32 tickets = 1; }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: No parameters.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [Integer]
docs.text: An array of order ticket numbers (Integer). Empty when nothing is open.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Much cheaper than opened_orders — use it for a fast heartbeat / change detector, then pull full detail only when the set changes.
  • Includes pendings. Tickets cover market and pending orders (same as opened_orders).
  • Diff pattern — keep the previous array and compare to spot new / closed tickets.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text:
tickets = acct.opened_orders_tickets
puts "open: #{tickets.size} → #{tickets.inspect}"

docs.title: 2) Detect changes between polls
docs.text:
prev = acct.opened_orders_tickets
loop do
  sleep 2
  now = acct.opened_orders_tickets
  (now - prev).each { |t| puts "opened  ##{t}" }
  (prev - now).each { |t| puts "closed  ##{t}" }
  prev = now
end

docs.title: 3) Pull detail only for a specific ticket
docs.text:
want = acct.opened_orders_tickets.min   # e.g. the oldest
o = acct.opened_orders.find { |x| x.ticket == want }
puts o ? "#{o.symbol} #{o.lots} lots" : "gone"

docs.title: 📜 Orders History
docs.text:
Request: closed / deleted orders in a time window ([HistoryOrderInfo]), auto-paged. On MT4 this is the record of finished trades (there is no separate "deals" list).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#orders_history (alias order_history) (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: OrdersHistory

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: OrdersHistory(OrdersHistoryRequest) → OrdersHistoryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#orders_history(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Your closed-order history between two times, returned as one flat array (the SDK follows the page token for you).
  • Why you need it. P/L reports, trade journals, reconciliation, per-symbol or per-magic breakdowns.
  • Window. from_utc is required; to_utc defaults to now.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Closed / deleted orders in [from_utc, to_utc], auto-paged.
  # Returns [HistoryOrderInfo]; raises ApiError on failure.
  def orders_history(from_utc:, to_utc: Time.now.utc,
                     sort: :HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC, page_size: 1000) -> Array<Mt4TermApi::HistoryOrderInfo>
  alias order_history orders_history
end

Request message:

OrdersHistoryRequest {
  EnumOrderHistorySortType input_sort_mode = 1;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp input_from      = 2;  // broker time
  google.protobuf.Timestamp input_from_utc  = 3;  // UTC   ← the SDK sets this
  google.protobuf.Timestamp input_to        = 4;  // broker time
  google.protobuf.Timestamp input_to_utc    = 5;  // UTC   ← the SDK sets this
  int32  page_number    = 6;
  int32  items_per_page = 7;
  string page_token     = 8;   // ← the SDK follows this to page
  int32  page_size      = 9;
}

Reply message: OrdersHistoryReply { oneof response { OrdersHistoryData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — OrdersHistoryData { repeated HistoryOrderInfo orders_info = 1; int32 total_count = 2; string next_page_token = 3; }. The SDK concatenates every page's orders_info and returns one array.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description from_utc Time / Integer / Timestamp required Window start (UTC). A Ruby Time is converted to Timestamp. to_utc Time / Integer / Timestamp Time.now.utc Window end (UTC). sort Symbol (EnumOrderHistorySortType) :HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC Server-side ordering. page_size Integer 1000 Rows per page request (paging is automatic).

docs.title: EnumOrderHistorySortType
docs.text:
enum EnumOrderHistorySortType {
  HISTORY_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC        = 0;
  HISTORY_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC       = 1;
  HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC       = 2;  // default
  HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC      = 3;
  HISTORY_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC  = 4;
  HISTORY_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC = 5;
}

The window is matched against each order's time per the chosen sort mode. The SDK sends the UTC bounds (input_from_utc / input_to_utc).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [HistoryOrderInfo]
docs.text:
Like OpenedOrderInfo, plus close (close_price / close_time) fields:

Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description ticket ticket Integer Order ticket. symbol symbol String Instrument. order_type order_type Symbol OpenedOrderType (same enum as open orders). lots lots Float Volume in lots. open_price open_price Float Entry price. close_price close_price Float Exit price. profit profit Float Realized P/L (account currency). swap swap Float Swap charged. commision commision Float Commission (proto spelling). stop_loss / take_profit stop_loss / take_profit Float SL / TP that were set. magic_number magic_number Integer EA magic number. comment comment String Order comment. open_time / open_time_utc … Timestamp Open time (broker / UTC). close_time / close_time_utc … Timestamp Close time (broker / UTC). account_login account_login Integer Owning account login.

docs.title: OpenedOrderType (on order_type)
docs.text:
enum OpenedOrderType {
  OO_OP_BUY       = 0;  // was a market order (position)
  OO_OP_SELL      = 1;  // was a market order (position)
  OO_OP_BUYLIMIT  = 2;  // was pending
  OO_OP_SELLLIMIT = 3;  // was pending
  OO_OP_BUYSTOP   = 4;  // was pending
  OO_OP_SELLSTOP  = 5;  // was pending
  OO_OP_BALANCE   = 6;  // non-trade book entry (deposit/withdrawal)
  OO_OP_CREDIT    = 7;  // non-trade book entry (credit)
}

(the input sort enum EnumOrderHistorySortType is listed in full under Input above.)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Auto-paged. You get one flat array; the SDK follows next_page_token until the server stops.
  • Longer deadline. History runs on a 120 s deadline (it can be large).
  • from_utc is required — pass a Time (converted for you); to_utc defaults to now.
  • Balance/credit rows can appear with order_type OO_OP_BALANCE / OO_OP_CREDIT — skip them for pure trade P/L.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Last 7 days, net P/L
docs.text:
hist = acct.orders_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
trades = hist.reject { |o| %i[OO_OP_BALANCE OO_OP_CREDIT].include?(o.order_type) }
puts "closed: #{trades.size}, net P/L #{trades.sum { |o| o.profit + o.swap + o.commision }.round(2)}"

docs.title: 2) Newest first
docs.text:
acct.orders_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 24 * 3600, sort: :HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC)
    .first(10).each { |o| puts format("#%d %-8s P/L %.2f", o.ticket, o.symbol, o.profit) }

docs.title: 3) Per-symbol breakdown
docs.text:
by_sym = acct.orders_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600).group_by(&:symbol)
by_sym.each { |sym, rows| puts "#{sym}: #{rows.size} trades, #{rows.sum(&:profit).round(2)}" }

docs.title: 4) Per-magic (strategy) P/L
docs.text:
acct.orders_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
    .group_by(&:magic_number)
    .each { |m, rows| puts "magic #{m}: #{rows.sum(&:profit).round(2)}" }

docs.title: 5) Error handling
docs.text:
def safe_history(acct, **win)
  acct.orders_history(**win)
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError, GRPC::BadStatus => e
  warn "orders_history failed: #{e.message}"
  []
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OpenedOrders — the currently open orders (full detail).
  • OpenedOrdersTickets — open tickets only.
  • Stats: TradeStats — aggregate performance over history.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#order_history.

docs.title: MT4Account · Orders & History — Overview
docs.text:
Everything about orders: what's open right now (market + pending), their tickets, and what's closed in history. On MT4 an open market order is the position.

These methods are read-only. All three live on mt4_term_api.AccountHelper. Each returns the raw *Data (read fields with snake_case accessors), or raises ApiError.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• OpenedOrders — all open orders in full detail ([OpenedOrderInfo]): ticket, symbol, order_type, lots, open price, SL/TP, profit, swap, commission, magic, comment. Market and pending in one list.
  • OpenedOrdersTickets — just the ticket numbers ([Integer]) — the lightweight way to poll "what's open".
  • OrdersHistory — closed / deleted orders in a time window ([HistoryOrderInfo]), auto-paged.

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English — MT4 orders model
docs.text:
MT4 has orders, not positions. There is one list of open orders; what kind each is comes from order_type:

order_type Meaning :OO_OP_BUY, :OO_OP_SELL Market orders — these are your open positions. :OO_OP_BUYLIMIT, :OO_OP_SELLLIMIT, :OO_OP_BUYSTOP, :OO_OP_SELLSTOP Pending orders — waiting to trigger. :OO_OP_BALANCE, :OO_OP_CREDIT Non-trade book entries (deposits / credit).

So "open positions" = opened_orders.select { |o| %i[OO_OP_BUY OO_OP_SELL].include?(o.order_type) }. The friendly MT4Service#positions / #pending_orders do this split for you.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Full detail of every open order opened_orders [OpenedOrderInfo] Only the tickets of open orders (cheap poll) opened_orders_tickets [Integer] Closed / deleted orders in a time window orders_history [HistoryOrderInfo]

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• One list, two kinds. opened_orders returns market and pending together — filter by order_type.
  • No separate deals. Unlike MT5, MT4 has no deals list; orders_history is the record of closed orders.
  • History is paged. orders_history auto-pages for you (follows next_page_token) and returns one flat array.
  • Window bounds are Timestamps on orders_history (sent as google.protobuf.Timestamp) — the SDK accepts a Ruby Time and converts.
  • commision spelling — the proto field is commision (single "m"), kept as-is.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
# Open market orders (= positions) and pending, split by type
all = acct.opened_orders
market  = all.select { |o| %i[OO_OP_BUY OO_OP_SELL].include?(o.order_type) }
pending = all.reject { |o| %i[OO_OP_BUY OO_OP_SELL OO_OP_BALANCE OO_OP_CREDIT].include?(o.order_type) }
puts "market #{market.size}, pending #{pending.size}"

# Cheap poll — just the tickets
puts "open tickets: #{acct.opened_orders_tickets.inspect}"

# Closed orders in the last 7 days
hist = acct.orders_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
puts "closed: #{hist.size}, net P/L #{hist.sum(&:profit).round(2)}"

docs.title: 📊 OHLC Bars
docs.text:
Request: OHLC price bars via QuoteHistory.Bars, oldest first, auto-paged. The modern history endpoint — prefer it over quote_history.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#bars (alias price_history) (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.QuoteHistory
  • Proto definition: Bars

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.QuoteHistory
  • Method: Bars(QuoteHistoryBarsRequest) → QuoteHistoryBarsReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::QuoteHistory::Stub#bars(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Candles (open/high/low/close + tick volume + spread) for a symbol and timeframe, over a time window.
  • Why you need it. Charts, indicators, backtests, volatility estimates.
  • Returns [QuoteHistoryBar] oldest-first; the SDK follows the page token and retries QUOTE_HISTORY_NOT_READY for you.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # OHLC bars, oldest first, auto-paged. `from_utc`/`to_utc` are UNIX SECONDS
  # (to_utc nil/0 = up to now). Returns [QuoteHistoryBar]; raises ApiError.
  def bars(symbol, timeframe: :M1, from_utc:, to_utc: nil,
           page_size: 1000, not_ready_retries: 10) -> Array<Mt4TermApi::QuoteHistoryBar>
  alias price_history bars
end

Request message:

QuoteHistoryBarsRequest {
  string symbol                 = 1;
  QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME timeframe = 2;
  int64  from_time              = 3;  // broker-time unix seconds
  int64  from_time_utc          = 4;  // UTC unix seconds   ← the SDK sets this
  int64  to_time                = 5;
  int64  to_time_utc            = 6;  // UTC unix seconds   ← the SDK sets this (0 = now)
  int32  page_size              = 7;
  string page_token             = 8;  // ← the SDK follows this to page
}

Reply message: QuoteHistoryBarsReply { oneof response { QuoteHistoryBarsData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — QuoteHistoryBarsData { repeated QuoteHistoryBar bars = 1; string next_page_token = 3; … }. The SDK concatenates all pages.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description symbol String required Symbol name. timeframe Symbol :M1 :M1 :M5 :M15 :M30 :H1 :H4 :D1 :W1 :MN1 (mapped to QHB_PERIOD_*). from_utc Integer / Time required Window start, UNIX SECONDS (a Time's .to_i). to_utc Integer / nil nil Window end, unix seconds; nil/0 = up to now. page_size Integer 1000 Bars per page (paging is automatic). not_ready_retries Integer 10 Retries on QUOTE_HISTORY_NOT_READY (1 s apart).

docs.title: QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME
docs.text:
enum QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME {       // value = minutes per bar
  QHB_PERIOD_M1 = 1;  QHB_PERIOD_M5  = 5;   QHB_PERIOD_M15 = 15;
  QHB_PERIOD_M30 = 30; QHB_PERIOD_H1 = 60;  QHB_PERIOD_H4  = 240;
  QHB_PERIOD_D1 = 1440; QHB_PERIOD_W1 = 10080; QHB_PERIOD_MN1 = 43200;
}

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [QuoteHistoryBar]
docs.text:
Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description time time Integer Bar open time, unix seconds (broker time zone). time_utc time_utc Integer Bar open time, unix seconds (UTC). open / high / low / close … Float OHLC prices. tick_volume tick_volume Integer Number of ticks in the bar. spread spread Integer Spread in points. real_volume real_volume Integer Real volume (usually 0 on MT4).

Times are plain unix seconds here (not Timestamp). Time.at(bar.time_utc).utc gives a Ruby time.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• from_utc is UNIX SECONDS, not a Timestamp — pass time.to_i or an epoch. (The legacy quote_history uses Timestamp instead.)
  • to_utc: 0 (or nil) means "up to now".
  • QUOTE_HISTORY_NOT_READY — the terminal fetches history from the broker on demand; the SDK retries automatically (not_ready_retries).
  • Newest N bars — easier via MT4Service#last_bars, which widens the window until enough bars exist.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Last day of M5
docs.text:
bars = acct.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :M5, from_utc: Time.now.to_i - 86_400)
puts "#{bars.size} bars, last close #{bars.last&.close}"

docs.title: 2) A fixed window
docs.text:
from = Time.utc(2026, 1, 1).to_i
to   = Time.utc(2026, 1, 8).to_i
acct.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, from_utc: from, to_utc: to).first(3).each do |b|
  puts "#{Time.at(b.time_utc).utc.strftime('%m-%d %H:%M')}  O#{b.open} C#{b.close}"
end

docs.title: 3) Simple ATR-style range
docs.text:
bars = acct.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, from_utc: Time.now.to_i - 24 * 3600)
avg = bars.map { |b| b.high - b.low }.then { |r| r.empty? ? 0 : r.sum / r.size }
puts "avg H1 range: #{avg.round(5)}"

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• QuoteHistory — the legacy (deprecated) bar endpoint.
  • Quote — the current tick.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#bars / #last_bars.

docs.title: 💱 Getting a Quote
docs.text:
Request: the last tick for one symbol (QuoteData: bid, ask, high, low, time). Prices come from here.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#quote (alias symbol_info_tick) (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: Quote

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: Quote(QuoteRequest) → QuoteReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#quote(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The latest bid/ask (plus session high/low and timestamps) for a single symbol.
  • Why you need it. Price before trading, spread checks, live dashboards.
  • Returns QuoteData. Read bid / ask with snake_case accessors.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Last tick for one symbol. Returns QuoteData; raises ApiError on failure.
  def quote(symbol) -> Mt4TermApi::QuoteData
  alias symbol_info_tick quote
end

Request message: QuoteRequest { string symbol = 1; }

Reply message: QuoteReply { oneof response { QuoteData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Description symbol String Symbol name, e.g. "EURUSD".

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — QuoteData
docs.text:
Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description symbol symbol String The symbol. bid bid Float Best bid. ask ask Float Best ask. high high Float Session high. low low Float Session low. date_time date_time Timestamp Tick time (broker time zone). date_time_utc date_time_utc Timestamp Tick time in UTC.

Spread = ask - bid. There is no last or volume field on MT4 QuoteData (those are MT5 tick fields).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Freshly added symbols can answer bid/ask = 0 for a moment — call symbol_select first and retry.
  • No last price — MT4 quotes carry bid/ask/high/low only.
  • Timestamps are Timestamp — read .seconds.
  • Many at once? Use quote_many instead of a loop.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Bid / ask / spread
docs.text:
q = acct.quote("EURUSD")
puts "bid #{q.bid}  ask #{q.ask}  spread #{(q.ask - q.bid).round(5)}"

docs.title: 2) Guard against a cold symbol
docs.text:
acct.symbol_select("XAUUSD")
q = acct.quote("XAUUSD")
q = acct.quote("XAUUSD") if q.bid.zero?   # one retry after select
puts "#{q.bid}/#{q.ask}"

docs.title: 3) Tick time in UTC
docs.text:
q = acct.quote("EURUSD")
puts "as of #{Time.at(q.date_time_utc.seconds).utc.iso8601}"

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• QuoteMany — several symbols in one call.
  • SymbolSelect — warm up a symbol first.
  • Streaming: OnSymbolTick — push ticks instead of polling.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#quote → a Quote struct with spread.

Back to: Symbols & Quotes — Overview · MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: 🕰️ Quote History (Legacy)
docs.text:
Request: OHLC bars via the legacy MarketInfo.QuoteHistory endpoint ([HistoryQuote]). Deprecated on the gateway and unpaged — prefer bars.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#quote_history (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: QuoteHistory

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: QuoteHistory(QuoteHistoryRequest) → QuoteHistoryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#quote_history(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The older history call. Same idea as bars, but it uses Timestamp windows, a different timeframe enum, and returns everything in one shot (no paging).
  • Why it's here. Compatibility with older code. For new code use bars.
  • Returns [HistoryQuote]. The SDK returns data.historical_quotes as an array.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Legacy MarketInfo.QuoteHistory (deprecated, unpaged). `from_utc`/`to_utc` are
  # Ruby Times (sent as Timestamp). Returns [HistoryQuote]; raises ApiError.
  def quote_history(symbol, timeframe: :M1, from_utc:, to_utc: Time.now.utc) -> Array<Mt4TermApi::HistoryQuote>
end

Request message:

QuoteHistoryRequest {
  string symbol                       = 1;
  ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME timeframe = 2;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp fromTime     = 3;  // broker time
  google.protobuf.Timestamp fromTimeUtc  = 4;  // UTC   ← the SDK sets this
  google.protobuf.Timestamp toTime       = 5;  // broker time
  google.protobuf.Timestamp toTimeUtc    = 6;  // UTC   ← the SDK sets this
}

Reply message: QuoteHistoryReply { oneof response { QuoteHistoryData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — QuoteHistoryData { repeated HistoryQuote historical_quotes = 1; }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description symbol String required Symbol name. timeframe Symbol :M1 :M1 … :MN1 (mapped to QH_PERIOD_*). from_utc Time / Integer required Window start (UTC) — sent as Timestamp. to_utc Time / Integer Time.now.utc Window end (UTC).

docs.title: ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME
docs.text:
enum ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME {   // note: ordinal values, not minutes
  QH_PERIOD_M1 = 0; QH_PERIOD_M5 = 1; QH_PERIOD_M15 = 2; QH_PERIOD_M30 = 3;
  QH_PERIOD_H1 = 4; QH_PERIOD_H4 = 5; QH_PERIOD_D1 = 6; QH_PERIOD_W1 = 7; QH_PERIOD_MN1 = 8;
}

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [HistoryQuote]
docs.text:
Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description symbol symbol String The symbol. index index Integer Bar index. time time Timestamp Bar time (broker time zone). time_utc time_utc Timestamp Bar time (UTC). open / high / low / close … Float OHLC prices. tick_volume tick_volume Integer Tick volume. real_volume real_volume Integer Real volume (usually 0 on MT4). spread spread Integer Spread in points.

Times are Timestamp here (.seconds), unlike bars which uses plain unix seconds.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prefer bars. This endpoint is deprecated, unpaged, and uses a different timeframe enum / time type. New code should call bars.
  • Window is Timestamp — pass a Ruby Time; the SDK converts.
  • No paging — a very wide window returns one large array (or may be capped server-side).
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Last day of H1 (legacy)
docs.text:
rows = acct.quote_history("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400)
puts "#{rows.size} bars, last close #{rows.last&.close}"

docs.title: 2) Read times
docs.text:
acct.quote_history("EURUSD", timeframe: :M15, from_utc: Time.now.utc - 3600).each do |b|
  puts "#{Time.at(b.time_utc.seconds).utc.strftime('%H:%M')}  C#{b.close}"
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• Bars — the modern, paged bar endpoint (use this).
  • Quote — the current tick.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#quote_history.

docs.title: 💱 Getting Many Quotes
docs.text:
Request: the last tick for several symbols in one call ([QuoteData]).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#quote_many (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: QuoteMany

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: QuoteMany(QuoteManyRequest) → QuoteManyReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#quote_many(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Bid/ask for a batch of symbols in a single round-trip.
  • Why you need it. A watchlist / dashboard — one call instead of N quote calls.
  • Returns [QuoteData]. Same fields as quote.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Last ticks for several symbols in one call. Returns [QuoteData]; raises ApiError.
  def quote_many(symbols) -> Array<Mt4TermApi::QuoteData>
end

Request message: QuoteManyRequest { repeated string symbols = 1; }

Reply message: QuoteManyReply { oneof response { QuoteManyData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — QuoteManyData { repeated QuoteData quotes = 1; }. The SDK returns quotes as an array.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Description symbols Array<String> (or a single String) Symbols to quote. The SDK wraps a lone string in an array.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [QuoteData]
docs.text: One QuoteData per symbol: symbol, bid, ask, high, low, date_time, date_time_utc. Order follows the request; a cold symbol may come back with bid/ask = 0.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Cheaper than a loop — one request, one response for the whole batch.
  • Warm up first — symbol_select each new symbol (or call tick_value_with_size, which adds them) to avoid 0/0.
  • Match by symbol — index the result by q.symbol, don't assume positional alignment if some are unknown.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Watchlist snapshot
docs.text:
acct.quote_many(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD USDJPY]).each do |q|
  puts format("%-8s %s / %s", q.symbol, q.bid, q.ask)
end

docs.title: 2) Index by symbol
docs.text:
by = acct.quote_many(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]).to_h { |q| [q.symbol, q] }
puts "EURUSD ask: #{by['EURUSD']&.ask}"

docs.title: 3) Spread scan
docs.text:
acct.quote_many(acct.symbols.first(20)).each do |q|
  spread = (q.ask - q.bid)
  puts "#{q.symbol}: #{spread.round(5)}" if spread.positive?
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• Quote — single-symbol version.
  • SymbolSelect — warm up symbols first.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#quote_many → Quote structs with spread.

Back to: Symbols & Quotes — Overview · MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: 🕒 Getting the Server Time Zone
docs.text:
Request: the broker server's UTC offset (ServerTimezoneData) from MT4. Answered cheaply from what the platform already knows.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#server_timezone (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.ServerTimezone
  • Proto definition: ServerTimezone (defined in mt4-term-api-server-timezone.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.ServerTimezone
  • Method: ServerTimezone(ServerTimezoneRequest) → ServerTimezoneReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::ServerTimezone::Stub#server_timezone(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The broker's offset from UTC, in seconds, plus how that figure was obtained.
  • Why you need it. Every *_utc field of the API is the broker server time minus this offset. Use it to convert broker timestamps to/from UTC, and to label chart times correctly.
  • Cheap. The platform answers from what it already knows — no round-trip to the broker.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Convert broker-local timestamps (server_time, bar time) to UTC and back.
  • Align candle / session boundaries with the broker's trading day.
  • Detect DST changes on the broker side (the offset shifts).

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Returns the broker server's UTC offset. Raises ApiError on failure.
  def server_timezone -> Mt4TermApi::ServerTimezoneData
end

Request message:

ServerTimezoneRequest {} (empty message — the SDK builds it; server_timezone takes no arguments)

Reply message:

ServerTimezoneReply {
  oneof response {
    ServerTimezoneData data = 1;
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: No parameters. The SDK sends an empty ServerTimezoneRequest.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — ServerTimezoneData
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description server server String Broker server / cluster name (e.g. "EGlobal-Demo"). utc_offset_seconds utc_offset_seconds Integer Broker server time minus UTC, in seconds (positive = ahead of UTC). source source Symbol How the offset was determined — see enum below. validated_utc validated_utc Timestamp When the offset was last validated (UTC). .seconds → unix seconds.

docs.title: SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE
docs.text:
enum SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE {
  SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_UNKNOWN        = 0;  // not determined yet
  SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LIVE           = 1;  // measured live against the server
  SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LAST_VALIDATED = 2;  // last known good value
}

tz = acct.server_timezone
fresh = tz.source == :SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LIVE

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Use it once, cache it. The offset rarely changes within a session (only on broker DST shifts). Read it after connect and reuse.
  • *_utc fields already applied it. Most API messages give you both broker-local and *_utc timestamps; you only need this call when you must convert a broker-local value yourself.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue for MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError.

docs.title: 1) Basic usage
docs.text:
tz = acct.server_timezone
hours = tz.utc_offset_seconds / 3600.0
puts "#{tz.server}: UTC#{hours >= 0 ? '+' : ''}#{hours}  (source #{tz.source})"

docs.title: 2) Convert a broker-local timestamp to UTC
docs.text:
tz = acct.server_timezone
broker_unix = acct.account_summary.server_time.seconds
utc = Time.at(broker_unix - tz.utc_offset_seconds).utc
puts "Broker time in UTC: #{utc.iso8601}"

docs.title: 3) Label bar times
docs.text:
tz = acct.server_timezone
bars = acct.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, from_utc: Time.now.to_i - 86_400)
bars.last(3).each do |b|
  # bars already carry time_utc; this shows the broker-local equivalent
  broker = Time.at(b.time_utc + tz.utc_offset_seconds).utc
  puts "#{broker.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')} (broker)  close #{b.close}"
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• AccountSummary — also carries server_time / server_time_utc / server_utc_offset_seconds.
  • Bars: Bars — OHLC history with time (broker) and time_utc.

docs.title: 🧾 Symbol Specifications
docs.text:
Request: the full specification of one symbol — or every symbol — in one call (SymbolParamsManyInfo): digits, point, volumes, contract size, margins, swaps, sessions and more.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#symbol_params_many (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: SymbolParamsMany

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: SymbolParamsMany(SymbolParamsManyRequest) → SymbolParamsManyReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#symbol_params_many(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The complete trading spec for a symbol: how many digits, the point size, min/max/step volume, contract size, margin and swap rules, session times.
  • Why you need it. Position sizing, rounding prices/volumes, validating stops, margin estimates.
  • One or all. Pass a symbol for a single spec; pass nothing for the whole book.

⚠️ PascalCase accessors. This message's fields are Capitalised: p.Digits, p.Point, p.VolumeMin, p.TradeContractSize, p.SymbolName… The friendly MT4Service#symbol_params returns a snake_case SymbolSpec struct instead.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # With `symbol`: that symbol's spec (SymbolParamsManyInfo) or nil if unknown.
  # Without `symbol`: ALL symbols' specs in one call ([SymbolParamsManyInfo]).
  def symbol_params_many(symbol = nil, timeout: 120)
end

Request message: SymbolParamsManyRequest { string symbol_name = 1; … } — the SDK sets symbol_name when you pass a symbol, or leaves it blank for all.

Reply message: SymbolParamsManyReply { oneof response { SymbolParamsManyData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — SymbolParamsManyData { repeated SymbolParamsManyInfo symbol_infos = 1; … }. With a symbol the SDK returns the matching info (or the first, or nil); without, the whole array.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description symbol String / nil nil One symbol's spec, or nil for all symbols. timeout Integer 120 Per-call deadline (the full list is large).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolParamsManyInfo (key fields)
docs.text:
The message carries ~60 fields; the ones you'll use most:

Identity & pricing

Accessor Type Description SymbolName String Symbol name. SymDescription String Human description. Path String Market Watch tree path. Digits Integer Price decimal places. Point Float Point size (10 ** -Digits). Bid Float Last bid. CurrencyBase / CurrencyProfit / CurrencyMargin String Base / profit / margin currencies.

Volumes & contract

Accessor Type Description VolumeMin / VolumeMax / VolumeStep Float Min / max / step lot size. TradeContractSize Float Units per lot (e.g. 100000). TradeTickValue / TradeTickSize Float Money per tick / price per tick.

Trading rules

Accessor Type Description TradeStopsLevel Integer Min SL/TP distance (points). TradeFreezeLevel Integer Freeze distance (points). TradeMode Symbol SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE — see below. TradeExeMode Symbol SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION — see below. TradeCalcMode Symbol SP_ENUM_TRADE_CALC_MODE — see below.

Swaps & margins

Accessor Type Description SwapLong / SwapShort Float Swap per long / short lot. MarginInitial / MarginMaintenance Float Initial / maintenance margin.

The full set (session volumes, limits, margin-rate variants, timestamps) is best explored offline: ruby examples/demos/helpers/17_protobuf_inspector.rb SymbolParamsManyInfo.

docs.title: SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE — TradeMode
docs.text:
enum SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE {
  SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_DISABLED  = 0;  // trading disabled
  SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_LONGONLY  = 1;  // buys only
  SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_SHORTONLY = 2;  // sells only
  SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_CLOSEONLY = 3;  // close positions only
  SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_FULL      = 4;  // full access
}

docs.title: SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION — TradeExeMode
docs.text:
enum SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION {
  SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_REQUEST  = 0;  // request execution
  SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_INSTANT  = 1;  // instant execution
  SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_MARKET   = 2;  // market execution
  SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_EXCHANGE = 3;  // exchange execution
}

docs.title: SP_ENUM_TRADE_CALC_MODE — TradeCalcMode
docs.text:
enum SP_ENUM_TRADE_CALC_MODE {
  SYMBOL_TRADE_MARGINE_CALC_MODE_FOREX   = 0;  // forex
  SYMBOL_TRADE_MARGINE_CALC_MODE_FUTURES = 1;  // futures
  SYMBOL_TRADE_MARGINE_CALC_MODE_CFD     = 2;  // CFD
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Round volumes to VolumeStep and clamp to [VolumeMin, VolumeMax] before order_send.
  • Respect TradeStopsLevel — SL/TP closer than this many points from price are rejected (mql_code 130).
  • Point vs pip — a 5-digit FX symbol's pip is 10 * Point.
  • Unknown symbol → nil (single) or absent from the array (all).
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) One symbol
docs.text:
p = acct.symbol_params_many("EURUSD")
puts "digits #{p.Digits}  point #{p.Point}  vol #{p.VolumeMin}–#{p.VolumeMax} step #{p.VolumeStep}"
puts "contract #{p.TradeContractSize}  min stop #{p.TradeStopsLevel} pts  mode #{p.TradeMode}"

docs.title: 2) Round a volume to the symbol's step
docs.text:
p = acct.symbol_params_many("EURUSD")
raw = 0.037
vol = ((raw / p.VolumeStep).floor * p.VolumeStep).clamp(p.VolumeMin, p.VolumeMax)
puts "rounded volume: #{vol}"

docs.title: 3) All symbols → a lookup
docs.text:
specs = acct.symbol_params_many.to_h { |p| [p.SymbolName, p] }
puts "XAUUSD contract: #{specs['XAUUSD']&.TradeContractSize}"

docs.title: 4) Tradable only
docs.text:
acct.symbol_params_many.select { |p| p.TradeMode == :SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_FULL }
    .first(5).each { |p| puts p.SymbolName }

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• TickValueWithSize — just the money-per-tick for sizing.
  • Quote — the live price.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#symbol_params → a snake_case SymbolSpec struct.
