docs.title: ➕ Market Watch — Select a Symbol
docs.text:
Request: add (or remove) a symbol from Market Watch so the terminal streams its quotes. Returns true/false.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#symbol_select (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolSelect

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolSelect(SymbolSelectRequest) → SymbolSelectReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_select(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Shows (select: true) or hides (select: false) a symbol in Market Watch.
  • Why you need it. A symbol must be selected before the terminal has a live quote for it — otherwise quote can briefly answer bid/ask = 0.
  • Returns Boolean — the SDK returns data.success.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Add (select=true) / remove a symbol from Market Watch. Returns true/false.
  def symbol_select(symbol, select = true) -> Boolean
end

Request message:

SymbolSelectRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  bool   select = 2;
}

Reply message: SymbolSelectReply { oneof response { SymbolSelectData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — SymbolSelectData { bool success = 1; }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description symbol String required Symbol name (e.g. "EURUSD"). select Boolean true true adds to Market Watch, false removes.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — Boolean
docs.text: true when the operation succeeded. Removing a symbol that has open orders / positions may return false.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Call it before quoting a fresh symbol. tick_value_with_size also adds symbols as a side effect.
  • Idempotent — selecting an already-selected symbol is fine.
  • Can't remove busy symbols — a symbol with open orders usually stays in Market Watch (false).
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Add then quote
docs.text:
acct.symbol_select("GBPUSD")
q = acct.quote("GBPUSD")
puts "#{q.bid}/#{q.ask}"

docs.title: 2) Ensure a set is watched
docs.text: %w[EURUSD GBPUSD USDJPY].each { |s| acct.symbol_select(s) }

docs.title: 3) Remove when done
docs.text:
ok = acct.symbol_select("GBPUSD", false)
puts ok ? "removed" : "still in use"

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• Quote — read the price after selecting.
  • Symbols — the full list of names.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#select_symbol.

Back to: Symbols & Quotes — Overview · MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: 🔤 Listing Symbols
docs.text:
Request: the names of all symbols the server offers ([String]).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#symbols (alias symbol_list) (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: Symbols

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: Symbols(SymbolsRequest) → SymbolsReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbols(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Every tradable symbol name known to the terminal (the broker's full list, not just Market Watch).
  • Why you need it. Validate a symbol exists, build a picker, iterate instruments.
  • Returns [String]. The SDK maps data.SymbolNameInfos to plain symbol-name strings.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Names of all symbols known to the terminal. Returns [String]; raises ApiError.
  def symbols -> Array<String>
  alias symbol_list symbols
end

Request message: SymbolsRequest {} (empty)

Reply message: SymbolsReply { oneof response { SymbolsData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — SymbolsData { repeated SymbolNameInfo SymbolNameInfos = 1; }, where SymbolNameInfo { string symbol_name; int32 symbol_index; }. The SDK returns the symbol_names.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: No parameters. Runs on a 120 s deadline (the list can be large).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [String]
docs.text:
An array of symbol names (e.g. "EURUSD", "XAUUSD", "#AA"). Order follows the server list.

Need the index alongside each name? Reach the raw reply via the generated stub, or read SymbolNameInfo.symbol_index.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Full broker list — not limited to Market Watch. A name being here doesn't mean it's selected; call symbol_select before quoting if bid/ask come back 0.
  • Membership check — acct.symbols.include?("EURUSD") is the MT4 way to ask "does it exist?" (there is no dedicated symbol_exist RPC; MT4Service#symbol_exist? wraps this).
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text:
names = acct.symbols
puts "total #{names.size}, first #{names.first}"

docs.title: 2) Does a symbol exist?
docs.text:
exists = acct.symbols.include?("EURUSD")
puts exists ? "yes" : "no"

docs.title: 3) Filter a family
docs.text:
usd = acct.symbols.select { |s| s.include?("USD") }
puts "USD pairs: #{usd.size}"

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolSelect — add a symbol to Market Watch before quoting.
  • Quote · QuoteMany — live prices.
  • SymbolParamsMany — full specs for all symbols.

Back to: Symbols & Quotes — Overview · MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: MT4Account · Symbols & Quotes — Overview
docs.text:
Everything market-data: the symbol list and Market Watch, live quotes (one or many), full symbol specs, tick value for sizing, OHLC bars, and the broker's time zone.

These methods are read-only except symbol_select (which toggles Market Watch). Quotes / symbols / bars live on mt4_term_api.MarketInfo and mt4_term_api.QuoteHistory; full specs and tick value on mt4_term_api.AccountHelper; the time zone on mt4_term_api.ServerTimezone. Each returns the raw *Data, or raises ApiError.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• Symbols — names of all symbols the server offers ([String]).
  • SymbolSelect — add / remove a symbol from Market Watch (Boolean).
  • Quote — the last tick for one symbol (QuoteData: bid, ask, high, low, time).
  • QuoteMany — last ticks for several symbols in one call ([QuoteData]).
  • SymbolParamsMany — the full specification of one symbol, or all (SymbolParamsManyInfo): digits, point, volumes, contract size, margins, swaps, sessions.
  • TickValueWithSize — tick value / tick size / contract size for position sizing.
  • Bars — OHLC bars via QuoteHistory.Bars, auto-paged.
  • QuoteHistory — the legacy MarketInfo.QuoteHistory bars (deprecated; prefer Bars).
  • ServerTimezone — the broker's UTC offset.

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• Need prices? → quote (one) or quote_many (several). Prices come from here.
  • Need the rules for sizing/stops? → symbol_params_many (full spec) or tick_value_with_size (just the money-per-tick).
  • Need history to chart or backtest? → bars (modern, paged). quote_history is the old endpoint kept for compatibility.
  • Need to convert broker times? → server_timezone.
  • A symbol answers 0/0? → it may not be in Market Watch yet — call symbol_select first.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns All symbol names symbols [String] Show/hide a symbol in Market Watch symbol_select Boolean Live price for one symbol quote QuoteData Live prices for many symbols quote_many [QuoteData] Full spec (digits, volumes, margins, swaps) symbol_params_many SymbolParamsManyInfo(s) Money value of one tick (sizing) tick_value_with_size [SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo] OHLC bars (chart / backtest) bars [QuoteHistoryBar] Legacy OHLC bars quote_history [HistoryQuote] Broker clock offset from UTC server_timezone ServerTimezoneData

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Add to Market Watch first. A symbol freshly referenced can answer bid/ask = 0 for a moment; symbol_select(sym) (and tick_value_with_size, which adds them too) warm it up.
  • Spec fields are PascalCase. SymbolParamsManyInfo uses p.Digits, p.Point, p.VolumeMin, p.TradeContractSize… (not snake_case). The friendly MT4Service#symbol_params returns a snake_case SymbolSpec struct.
  • Two bar endpoints. bars (QuoteHistory.Bars) is paged and uses unix-seconds from_utc/to_utc + QHB_PERIOD_* timeframes; quote_history (legacy) is unpaged and uses Timestamp + QH_PERIOD_*. Prefer bars.
  • QUOTE_HISTORY_NOT_READY. The terminal fetches history on demand; bars retries this automatically.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
# Price for one symbol
q = acct.quote("EURUSD")
puts "bid #{q.bid} ask #{q.ask}"

# Full spec (PascalCase accessors)
p = acct.symbol_params_many("EURUSD")
puts "digits #{p.Digits}  vol_min #{p.VolumeMin}  contract #{p.TradeContractSize}"

# Last 100 M5 bars
bars = acct.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :M5, from_utc: Time.now.to_i - 86_400)
puts "#{bars.size} bars, last close #{bars.last&.close}"

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used in Symbols & Quotes
docs.text:
Where Enum Values bars(timeframe:) QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME :QHB_PERIOD_M1 (1) · _M5 (5) · _M15 (15) · _M30 (30) · _H1 (60) · _H4 (240) · _D1 (1440) · _W1 (10080) · _MN1 (43200) — value = minutes quote_history(timeframe:) ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME :QH_PERIOD_M1 (0) · _M5 (1) · _M15 (2) · _M30 (3) · _H1 (4) · _H4 (5) · _D1 (6) · _W1 (7) · _MN1 (8)

You pass the friendly symbol (:M1 … :MN1) to bars / quote_history; the SDK maps it to the right enum. The SymbolParamsManyInfo spec also carries TradeMode / TradeCalcMode / TradeExeMode enums (see SymbolParamsMany).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Account: Account Information — Overview.
  • Trading: Trading Operations — Overview.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#quote / #symbol_params / #bars.

docs.title: 💵 Tick Value & Size
docs.text:
Request: the tick value / tick size / contract size for one or more symbols — the money-per-tick you need for position sizing.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#tick_value_with_size (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: TickValueWithSize

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: TickValueWithSize(TickValueWithSizeRequest) → TickValueWithSizeReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#tick_value_with_size(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. For each requested symbol: the monetary value of one tick, the tick size, and the contract size.
  • Why you need it. Risk-based sizing: convert a stop distance (in ticks/points) into money, then into lots. MT4 has no server-side margin/profit calc RPC, so this is the sizing primitive.
  • Returns [SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo]. The SDK returns data.infos as an array. Selecting the symbols is a side effect (they're added to Market Watch).

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Tick value / size / contract size for named symbols (adds them to Market Watch).
  # Returns [SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo]; raises ApiError on failure.
  def tick_value_with_size(symbols) -> Array<Mt4TermApi::SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo>
end

Request message: TickValueWithSizeRequest { repeated string symbol_names = 1; }

Reply message: TickValueWithSizeReply { oneof response { TickValueWithSizeData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — TickValueWithSizeData { repeated SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo infos = 1; }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Description symbols Array<String> (or a single String) Symbols to measure. The SDK wraps a lone string in an array.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo]
docs.text:
Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description index index Integer Position in the request. symbolName symbolName String Symbol (camelCase accessor). TradeTickValue TradeTickValue Float Money value of one tick per 1.0 lot (account currency). TradeTickSize TradeTickSize Float Price change of one tick. TradeContractSize TradeContractSize Float Units per lot.

PascalCase/camelCase accessors — symbolName, TradeTickValue, TradeTickSize, TradeContractSize.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Sizing formula. Risk money ÷ (stop distance in ticks × TradeTickValue) = lots. Round to the symbol's VolumeStep (from symbol_params_many).
  • Pip vs tick. On a 5-/3-digit symbol a pip is 10 ticks — scale TradeTickValue accordingly for pip-based risk.
  • Side effect: requested symbols are added to Market Watch (handy before quoting).
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Read tick value
docs.text:
info = acct.tick_value_with_size("EURUSD").first
puts "tick value #{info.TradeTickValue}  tick size #{info.TradeTickSize}  contract #{info.TradeContractSize}"

docs.title: 2) Lots for a fixed money risk
docs.text:
def lots_for_risk(acct, symbol, risk_money, stop_ticks)
  tv = acct.tick_value_with_size(symbol).first.TradeTickValue
  p  = acct.symbol_params_many(symbol)
  raw = risk_money / (stop_ticks * tv)
  ((raw / p.VolumeStep).floor * p.VolumeStep).clamp(p.VolumeMin, p.VolumeMax)
end
puts lots_for_risk(acct, "EURUSD", 50.0, 200)   # risk $50 over a 200-tick stop

docs.title: 3) Batch
docs.text:
acct.tick_value_with_size(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD XAUUSD]).each do |i|
  puts format("%-8s tick value %.2f", i.symbolName, i.TradeTickValue)
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolParamsMany — full spec incl. volume step for rounding.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Sugar#pip_value / #max_lot / #required_margin — local sizing helpers built on this.

Back to: Symbols & Quotes — Overview · MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: 🔁 Close By (Opposite Order)
docs.text:
Request: close one market order by an opposite one on the same symbol — netting them out in a single operation. Returns OrderCloseByData.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#order_close_by (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderCloseBy

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderCloseBy(OrderCloseByRequest) → OrderCloseByReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::TradingHelper::Stub#order_close_by(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closes a buy against a sell (or vice-versa) on the same symbol in one shot, instead of closing each at market.
  • Why you need it. Net out a hedge; exit both legs at one price; avoid paying the spread twice.
  • Returns OrderCloseByData (close_price, profit, close_time). A rejection raises ApiError.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Close one market order by an opposite one on the same symbol.
  # Returns OrderCloseByData; raises ApiError on rejection.
  def order_close_by(ticket:, opposite_ticket:) -> Mt4TermApi::OrderCloseByData
end

Request message:

OrderCloseByRequest {
  int32 ticket_to_close            = 1;
  int32 opposite_ticket_closing_by = 2;
}

Reply message: OrderCloseByReply { oneof response { OrderCloseByData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Description ticket Integer required The order to close (ticket_to_close). opposite_ticket Integer required The opposite-direction order on the same symbol that closes it (opposite_ticket_closing_by).

Both tickets must be open market orders, on the same symbol, in opposite directions (one buy, one sell).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseByData
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description close_price close_price Float Price at which the pair was closed. profit profit Float Realized P/L of the operation. close_time close_time Timestamp Close time (broker time zone). close_time_utc close_time_utc Timestamp Close time (UTC).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Same symbol, opposite side — mismatched symbols or same-direction tickets are rejected.
  • Unequal volumes — the larger order is partially closed; a remainder order may stay open.
  • Guard with rescue — either ticket may already be closed → ApiError.
  • Exactly once — a transport failure raises TradeOutcomeUnknown; check before retrying.

docs.title: 1) Net out a hedge
docs.text:
buy  = acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy,  volume: 0.10)
sell = acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :sell, volume: 0.10)
out  = acct.order_close_by(ticket: buy.ticket, opposite_ticket: sell.ticket)
puts "closed by @ #{out.close_price}, P/L #{out.profit.round(2)}"

docs.title: 2) Find an opposite order automatically
docs.text:
MARKET = %i[OO_OP_BUY OO_OP_SELL]
orders = acct.opened_orders.select { |o| MARKET.include?(o.order_type) && o.symbol == "EURUSD" }
buy  = orders.find { |o| o.order_type == :OO_OP_BUY }
sell = orders.find { |o| o.order_type == :OO_OP_SELL }
acct.order_close_by(ticket: buy.ticket, opposite_ticket: sell.ticket) if buy && sell

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OrderCloseDelete — close / delete a single order.
  • OrderSend — open the legs first.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Sugar#close_by.

Back to: Trading Operations — Overview · MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: 🔴 Closing / Deleting an Order
docs.text:
Request: close a market order (full or partial) or delete a pending order, by ticket. Returns OrderCloseDeleteData (mode, history_order_comment).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#order_close (aliases order_close_delete, order_delete) (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderCloseDelete

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderCloseDelete(OrderCloseDeleteRequest) → OrderCloseDeleteReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::TradingHelper::Stub#order_close_delete(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One call that closes a market order or deletes a pending one — the server decides which by the ticket's type and tells you via mode.
  • Why you need it. Exit trades; cancel pendings; take partial profits.
  • Returns OrderCloseDeleteData. A rejection raises ApiError.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Close a market order (lots nil = full, else partial) or delete a pending order.
  # Returns OrderCloseDeleteData (mode, history_order_comment); raises ApiError.
  def order_close(ticket:, lots: nil, price: nil, slippage: 10) -> Mt4TermApi::OrderCloseDeleteData
  alias order_close_delete order_close
  alias order_delete order_close
end

Request message:

OrderCloseDeleteRequest {
  int32  order_ticket  = 1;
  double lots          = 2;  // nil/omit = full close; a value = partial close
  double closing_price = 3;  // optional; gateway uses the current quote if omitted
  int32  slippage      = 4;  // points
}

Reply message: OrderCloseDeleteReply { oneof response { OrderCloseDeleteData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description ticket Integer required Order to close / delete (order_ticket). lots Float nil Partial close volume; nil closes the whole order. Ignored when deleting a pending. price Float nil Closing price (closing_price); omit to use the current quote. slippage Integer 10 Max slippage in points (market close).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseDeleteData
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description mode mode Symbol What happened — OrderCloseDeleteMode (below). history_order_comment history_order_comment String The comment recorded on the resulting history order.

docs.title: OrderCloseDeleteMode
docs.text:
enum OrderCloseDeleteMode {
  OCD_MARKET_ORDER  = 0;  // a market order was CLOSED
  OCD_PENDING_ORDER = 1;  // a pending order was DELETED
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Full vs partial. Omit lots to close everything; pass lots: 0.05 to close part of a 0.10 position (the remainder stays open with a new ticket).
  • mode tells you the kind. :OCD_MARKET_ORDER = a position was closed; :OCD_PENDING_ORDER = a pending was deleted.
  • Deleting a pending — just pass its ticket; lots/price/slippage are ignored.
  • Guard with rescue — a ticket may already be gone (filled/closed) → ApiError.
  • Exactly once — a transport failure raises TradeOutcomeUnknown; check before retrying.

docs.title: 1) Full close
docs.text:
out = acct.order_close(ticket: 465_423_938)
puts "closed (#{out.mode})"            # OCD_MARKET_ORDER

docs.title: 2) Partial close
docs.text: acct.order_close(ticket: 465_423_938, lots: 0.05)   # halve a 0.10 position

docs.title: 3) Delete a pending order
docs.text:
out = acct.order_delete(ticket: 465_424_047)
puts "deleted (#{out.mode})"           # OCD_PENDING_ORDER

docs.title: 4) Close every market order
docs.text:
MARKET = %i[OO_OP_BUY OO_OP_SELL]
acct.opened_orders.select { |o| MARKET.include?(o.order_type) }.each do |o|
  acct.order_close(ticket: o.ticket)
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError => e
  warn "##{o.ticket}: #{e.code}"
end

docs.text:

  • OrderCloseBy — net out two opposite orders.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Sugar#close_order / #cancel_order / #close_all.

docs.title: ✏️ Modifying an Order
docs.text:
Request: change the SL / TP of a market order, or the price / SL / TP / expiration of a pending order. Returns OrderModifyData (order_was_modified).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#order_modify (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderModify

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderModify(OrderModifyRequest) → OrderModifyReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::TradingHelper::Stub#order_modify(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Updates SL/TP (and, for pendings, price & expiration) of an existing order by ticket.
  • Why you need it. Trailing stops, break-even moves, retargeting a pending order.
  • Returns OrderModifyData — check order_was_modified. A rejection raises ApiError.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Modify SL/TP (market) or price/SL/TP/expiration (pending). Only the fields you pass change.
  # Returns OrderModifyData (order_was_modified); raises ApiError on rejection.
  def order_modify(ticket:, stop_loss: nil, take_profit: nil, price: nil, expiration_utc: nil) -> Mt4TermApi::OrderModifyData
end

Request message:

OrderModifyRequest {
  int32  order_ticket                    = 1;
  double new_price                       = 2;  // pending only
  double new_stop_loss                   = 3;
  double new_take_profit                 = 4;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp new_expiration     = 5; // broker time
  google.protobuf.Timestamp new_expiration_utc = 6; // UTC ← the SDK sets this
}

Reply message: OrderModifyReply { oneof response { OrderModifyData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — OrderModifyData { bool order_was_modified = 1; }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Description ticket Integer required The order to modify (order_ticket). stop_loss Float nil New SL price (new_stop_loss). take_profit Float nil New TP price (new_take_profit). price Float nil New pending price (new_price). Ignored for market orders. expiration_utc Time nil New pending expiry (UTC; sent as Timestamp).

Only the fields you pass are set on the request; omit the rest.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderModifyData
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description order_was_modified order_was_modified Boolean true when the change was applied.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Respect TradeStopsLevel. SL/TP closer than the symbol's stops level raises mql_code 130.
  • "No changes" rejection. Re-sending identical SL/TP can be refused (mql_code 1); only modify when the value actually changes (trailing-stop ratchet pattern).
  • Market vs pending. price only applies to pending orders.
  • Errors are exceptions: wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 1) Attach SL/TP to a market order
docs.text: acct.order_modify(ticket: 465_423_938, stop_loss: 1.0800, take_profit: 1.1000)

docs.title: 2) Move stop to break-even
docs.text:
o = acct.opened_orders.find { |x| x.ticket == 465_423_938 }
acct.order_modify(ticket: o.ticket, stop_loss: o.open_price) if o

docs.title: 3) Trailing-stop ratchet (never loosen)
docs.text:
best = nil
loop do
  sleep 1
  bid  = acct.quote("EURUSD").bid
  want = (bid - 150 * 0.0001).round(5)
  if best.nil? || want > best
    best = want
    acct.order_modify(ticket: 465_423_938, stop_loss: want)
  end
end

docs.title: 4) Re-price a pending order
docs.text: acct.order_modify(ticket: 465_424_047, price: 1.0950)

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OrderSend — open the order first.
  • OrderCloseDelete — close / delete.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Sugar#modify_sl / #modify_sl_tp.

docs.title: 🟢 Sending an Order
docs.text:
Request: open a market or pending order. Returns OrderSendData — a ticket > 0 means filled. A rejection raises ApiError (MT4 has no retcode).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#order_send (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderSend

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderSend(OrderSendRequest) → OrderSendReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::TradingHelper::Stub#order_send(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Places a buy/sell at market, or a pending limit/stop order.
  • Why you need it. Entering trades — the core write operation.
  • Success = ticket. OrderSendData.ticket > 0 is the filled/placed order id. There is no returned_code.
  • Rejection raises. Broker refusals come back as ApiError with an mql_code (130, 132, 134…). Wrap in begin/rescue.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Market or pending order. `type` is a friendly symbol (mapped to OC_OP_*).
  # `price` is ignored for market orders; `slippage` is in points; `magic` -> magic_number.
  # Returns OrderSendData (ticket, volume, price, open_time); raises ApiError on rejection.
  def order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, price: nil, stop_loss: nil, take_profit: nil,
                 comment: nil, magic: nil, slippage: nil, expiration_utc: nil) -> Mt4TermApi::OrderSendData
end

Request message:

OrderSendRequest {
  string symbol                   = 1;
  OrderSendOperationType operation_type = 2;  // OC_OP_* (SDK maps :buy → :OC_OP_BUY)
  double volume                   = 3;        // lots
  double price                    = 4;        // pending price (ignored for market)
  int32  slippage                 = 5;        // points
  double stoploss                 = 6;
  double takeprofit               = 7;
  string comment                  = 8;
  int32  magic_number             = 9;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration     = 10; // broker time
  google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration_utc = 11; // UTC ← the SDK sets this
}

Reply message: OrderSendReply { oneof response { OrderSendData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description symbol String required Instrument, e.g. "EURUSD". type Symbol required :buy :sell :buy_limit :sell_limit :buy_stop :sell_stop (mapped to OC_OP_*). volume Float required Lots (respect VolumeMin/Max/Step). price Float nil Pending-order price. Ignored for market orders (gateway uses the current quote). stop_loss Float nil SL price. take_profit Float nil TP price. comment String nil Order comment. magic Integer nil EA magic number (magic_number). slippage Integer nil Max slippage in points. expiration_utc Time nil Pending-order expiry (UTC; sent as Timestamp).

docs.title: OrderSendOperationType
docs.text:
enum OrderSendOperationType {
  OC_OP_BUY       = 0;  // ← :buy
  OC_OP_SELL      = 1;  // ← :sell
  OC_OP_BUYLIMIT  = 2;  // ← :buy_limit
  OC_OP_SELLLIMIT = 3;  // ← :sell_limit
  OC_OP_BUYSTOP   = 4;  // ← :buy_stop
  OC_OP_SELLSTOP  = 5;  // ← :sell_stop
}

Friendly vs raw. type: :buy works because the SDK maps it to :OC_OP_BUY. If you build the protobuf yourself you must use :OC_OP_BUY — the raw field rejects :buy.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderSendData
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description ticket ticket Integer The new order's ticket (> 0 = success). volume volume Float Filled / placed volume. price price Float Fill price (market) or order price (pending). open_time open_time Timestamp Open time (broker time zone). open_time_utc open_time_utc Timestamp Open time (UTC).

docs.title: 🚨 Errors — no retcode, exceptions instead
docs.text:
A broker rejection raises MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError; read e.mql_code:

mql_code Meaning 130 Invalid stops (SL/TP too close — see TradeStopsLevel). 131 Invalid volume. 132 Market closed. 134 Not enough money. 138 Requote (price moved). 148 Too many orders.

A transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal raises TradeOutcomeUnknown (mixed into the gRPC error) — the trade is not re-sent; check open orders before retrying.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Round volume to the symbol's VolumeStep; keep SL/TP beyond TradeStopsLevel points.
  • Market vs pending — pass price: only for *_limit / *_stop types.
  • magic tags your orders so you can filter them later (opened_orders / orders_history).
  • 120 s deadline — trade calls use a longer timeout.

docs.title: 1) Market buy
docs.text:
r = acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.10, magic: 600_101, comment: "entry")
puts "ticket ##{r.ticket} @ #{r.price}"

docs.title: 2) Market buy with SL/TP
docs.text:
q = acct.quote("EURUSD")
r = acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.10,
                    stop_loss: (q.bid - 0.0020).round(5),
                    take_profit: (q.ask + 0.0020).round(5))

docs.title: 3) Pending buy-limit below the market
docs.text:
q = acct.quote("EURUSD")
acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy_limit, volume: 0.10, price: (q.bid - 0.0050).round(5))

docs.title: 4) Safe send with rejection handling
docs.text:
def safe_buy(acct, sym, vol)
  acct.order_send(symbol: sym, type: :buy, volume: vol)
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::TradeOutcomeUnknown => e
  warn "UNKNOWN outcome for #{e.operation} — check open orders!"
  nil
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError => e
  warn "rejected: #{e.code} (mql #{e.mql_code})"
  nil
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OrderModify — attach / change SL/TP afterwards.
  • OrderCloseDelete — close or delete.
  • OpenedOrders — confirm what's open.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Sugar#buy_market / #buy_market_with_sl_tp.

docs.title: MT4Account · Trading Operations — Overview
docs.text:
The four order RPCs: send a market or pending order, modify its SL/TP/price, close or delete it, and close one order by an opposite one.

All four live on mt4_term_api.TradingHelper. Each returns the raw *Data, or raises ApiError on rejection. These are the only methods that place or change orders.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• OrderSend — open a market or pending order (OrderSendData: ticket, price, volume).
  • OrderModify — change SL / TP (market) or price / SL / TP / expiration (pending) → OrderModifyData.
  • OrderCloseDelete — close a market order (full / partial) or delete a pending one → OrderCloseDeleteData.
  • OrderCloseBy — close one market order by an opposite one on the same symbol → OrderCloseByData.

docs.title: ⚠️ MT4 trade contract — read this first
docs.text:
• No retcode. Unlike MT5 there is no returned_code. order_send returns OrderSendData with a ticket > 0 when filled. A rejection raises MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError — read e.mql_code.
  • Common mql_code rejections: 130 invalid stops, 131 invalid volume, 132 market closed, 134 not enough money, 138 requote, 148 too many orders.
  • Exactly once. A trade call is never re-sent by the SDK. A transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal is raised as TradeOutcomeUnknown (mixed into the gRPC error) — check your open orders before retrying. See Return Codes.
  • An order IS the position. Closing a market order closes the position; "deleting" applies to pending orders.

docs.title: 🧭 Order types — two different enums
docs.text:
Context Enum Values Sending an order (order_send) OrderSendOperationType OC_OP_BUY (0) · OC_OP_SELL (1) · OC_OP_BUYLIMIT (2) · OC_OP_SELLLIMIT (3) · OC_OP_BUYSTOP (4) · OC_OP_SELLSTOP (5) Reading open orders (opened_orders) OpenedOrderType OO_OP_BUY (0) · OO_OP_SELL (1) · OO_OP_BUYLIMIT (2) … OO_OP_BALANCE (6) · OO_OP_CREDIT (7)

Friendly aliases. order_send(type: :buy) is mapped by the SDK to :OC_OP_BUY. The raw protobuf field needs the full :OC_OP_* symbol — :buy only works because the method translates it. Accepted friendly types: :buy :sell :buy_limit :sell_limit :buy_stop :sell_stop.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Open a market / pending order order_send OrderSendData Change SL / TP / price / expiration order_modify OrderModifyData Close a market order / delete a pending one order_close_delete OrderCloseDeleteData Net out two opposite orders on one symbol order_close_by OrderCloseByData

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
# Market buy 0.10 lots
r = acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.10, magic: 600_101)
puts "filled ticket ##{r.ticket} @ #{r.price}"

# Attach SL/TP, then close
acct.order_modify(ticket: r.ticket, stop_loss: 1.0800, take_profit: 1.1000)
out = acct.order_close_delete(ticket: r.ticket)   # full close
puts "closed (#{out.mode})"

# Handle a rejection
begin
  acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.10, stop_loss: 1.5)
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError => e
  puts "rejected: #{e.code} (mql #{e.mql_code})"   # e.g. 130 invalid stops
end

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Read orders: Orders & History — Overview.
  • Sizing: TickValueWithSize · SymbolParamsMany.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Sugar — buy_market, close_order, buy_market_with_sl_tp, …

docs.title: 🔌 Streaming Connect-State
docs.text:
Stream: the terminal's connection state as it changes. Yields ConnectStateData on a background thread. Lives on the Connection service (not SubscriptionService).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#on_connect_state (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.Connection
  • Proto definition: OnConnectState (server-streaming)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.Connection
  • Method: OnConnectState(OnConnectStateRequest) → stream OnConnectStateReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::Connection::Stub#on_connect_state(request, metadata:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A push stream that reports the terminal's link health — connected / alive / server / last error — whenever it changes.
  • Why you need it. Watchdog: detect a dropped broker link, surface reconnect status, drive an "online" indicator.
  • Yields ConnectStateData.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Terminal connect-state changes. `terminal_ids` is a repeated field; defaults to
  # this client's own id (accepts a single id or an array). Yields ConnectStateData
  # on a background thread. Returns a Subscription; call .cancel to stop.
  def on_connect_state(terminal_ids = @id) { |state| ... } -> MetaRPC::MT4::Subscription
end

Request message: OnConnectStateRequest { repeated string terminal_ids = 1; }

terminal_ids is REPEATED. The SDK wraps your value with Array(...), so on_connect_state("id"), on_connect_state(["id1","id2"]), or the default (this client's own id) all work.

Reply (stream): OnConnectStateReply { ConnectStateData data; … }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description terminal_ids String / Array<String> this client's id Which terminal(s) to watch. &block block — Called with each ConnectStateData.

docs.title: ⬆️ Yielded — ConnectStateData
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description id id String Terminal session id this state is for. state state String Human-readable state (e.g. "Connected"). is_connected is_connected Boolean Linked to the broker. is_alive is_alive Boolean Terminal process alive. api_is_alive api_is_alive Boolean API bridge alive. server server String Broker server / cluster. account account Integer Account login. error_message error_message String Last error, if any. timestamp timestamp Timestamp When this state was observed.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Different service. Unlike the other streams, this one is on mt4_term_api.Connection.
  • Defaults to your terminal — omit terminal_ids to watch the one you connected.
  • Pairs with reconnect — on is_connected == false, you might call reconnect and keep watching.
  • Returns a Subscription — sub.cancel to stop; don't cancel inside the block.

docs.title: 1) Watch link health
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_connect_state do |st|
  puts "#{st.state}  connected=#{st.is_connected} alive=#{st.is_alive} server=#{st.server}"
end
sleep 10
sub.cancel

docs.title: 2) Alert on disconnect
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_connect_state do |st|
  warn "⚠️ link down: #{st.error_message}" unless st.is_connected
end
sleep 30
sub.cancel

docs.title: 3) Watch several terminals
docs.text:
ids = acct.accounts.map(&:id) rescue [acct.id]
sub = acct.on_connect_state(ids) { |st| puts "#{st.id}: #{st.state}" }
sleep 5
sub.cancel

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• Health checks (one-shot): check_connect / connect_state / connection_status — see Constructor & connection.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#on_connect_state.

Back to: Streaming Methods — Overview · MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: 💰 Streaming Open-Orders Profit
docs.text:
Stream: the floating P/L of every open order, pushed on a timer. Yields OnOpenedOrdersProfitData on a background thread.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#on_opened_orders_profit (alias on_position_profit) (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnOpenedOrdersProfit (server-streaming)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnOpenedOrdersProfit(OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest) → stream OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::SubscriptionService::Stub#on_opened_orders_profit(request, metadata:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A periodic push (every interval_ms) of each open order's current profit, plus a live account snapshot.
  • Why you need it. A live P/L panel without polling opened_orders in a loop.
  • Yields OnOpenedOrdersProfitData.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Open orders' P/L every `interval_ms`. Yields OnOpenedOrdersProfitData on a
  # background thread. Returns a Subscription; call .cancel to stop.
  def on_opened_orders_profit(interval_ms: 1000) { |data| ... } -> MetaRPC::MT4::Subscription
  alias on_position_profit on_opened_orders_profit
end

Request message: OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest { int32 timer_period_milliseconds = 1; }

Reply (stream): OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply { OnOpenedOrdersProfitData data; … }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description interval_ms Integer 1000 Push period in milliseconds (timer_period_milliseconds). &block block — Called with each OnOpenedOrdersProfitData.

docs.title: ⬆️ Yielded — OnOpenedOrdersProfitData
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description type type Symbol Event group (MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE). opened_orders_with_profit_updated … [OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo] One row per open order (see below). account_info account_info OnEventAccountInfo Live account snapshot. terminal_instance_guid_id terminal_instance_guid_id String Terminal session id.

docs.title: OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo (per order)
docs.text: Field Type Description ticket Integer Order ticket. symbol String Instrument. type Symbol SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE. lots Float Volume. open_price Float Entry price. order_profit Float Current floating P/L (note: order_profit, not profit). swap Float Accrued swap. commission Float Commission (here spelled commission, double "s"). stop_loss / take_profit Float SL / TP. magic_number Integer EA magic. comment String Order comment. open_time / open_time_utc Timestamp Open time.

docs.title: MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE (on type)
docs.text:
enum MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE {
  OrderProfit = 0;  // a periodic profit update (this stream)
  OrderUpdate = 1;  // an order opened / modified / closed
}

docs.title: SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE (on each order's type)
docs.text:
enum SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE {
  SUB_OP_BUY       = 0;
  SUB_OP_SELL      = 1;
  SUB_OP_BUYLIMIT  = 2;
  SUB_OP_SELLLIMIT = 3;
  SUB_OP_BUYSTOP   = 4;
  SUB_OP_SELLSTOP  = 5;
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Field name is order_profit on the streamed rows (the static opened_orders list uses profit).
  • Commission spelling differs — commission here vs commision on OpenedOrderInfo.
  • Tune interval_ms — 1000 ms is plenty for a UI; lower it only if you really need sub-second updates.
  • Returns a Subscription — sub.cancel to stop; don't cancel inside the block.

docs.title: 1) Live total floating P/L
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_opened_orders_profit(interval_ms: 1000) do |d|
  total = d.opened_orders_with_profit_updated.sum(&:order_profit)
  puts "floating P/L: #{total.round(2)}  (equity #{d.account_info.equity.round(2)})"
end
sleep 10
sub.cancel

docs.title: 2) Per-order rows
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_opened_orders_profit do |d|
  d.opened_orders_with_profit_updated.each do |o|
    puts format("#%d %-8s %.2f", o.ticket, o.symbol, o.order_profit)
  end
end
sleep 5
sub.cancel

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OnOpenedOrdersTickets — ticket snapshots on a timer.
  • OpenedOrders — full detail (poll).
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#on_opened_orders_profit.

docs.title: 🎟️ Streaming Ticket Snapshots
docs.text:
Stream: the open ticket numbers (positions + pendings) pushed on a timer. Yields OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData on a background thread.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#on_opened_orders_tickets (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnOpenedOrdersTickets (server-streaming)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnOpenedOrdersTickets(OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) → stream OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::SubscriptionService::Stub#on_opened_orders_tickets(request, metadata:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A lightweight periodic push of just the open tickets — split into positions and pending orders.
  • Why you need it. Cheaply detect when an order opens / closes without pushing full records; drive a "diff" against your last snapshot.
  • Yields OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Open order tickets every `interval_ms`. Yields OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData on a
  # background thread. Returns a Subscription; call .cancel to stop.
  def on_opened_orders_tickets(interval_ms: 1000) { |data| ... } -> MetaRPC::MT4::Subscription
end

Request message: OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest { int32 pull_interval_milliseconds = 1; }

Reply (stream): OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply { OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData data; … }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Default Description interval_ms Integer 1000 Push period in milliseconds (pull_interval_milliseconds). &block block — Called with each OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData.

docs.title: ⬆️ Yielded — OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData
docs.text:
Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description position_tickets position_tickets [Integer] Tickets of open market orders (positions). pending_order_tickets pending_order_tickets [Integer] Tickets of open pending orders. server_time server_time Timestamp Snapshot time (broker time zone). server_time_utc server_time_utc Timestamp Snapshot time (UTC). terminal_instance_guid_id terminal_instance_guid_id String Terminal session id.

Note: this stream separates positions from pendings (unlike the one-shot opened_orders_tickets, which returns a single combined array).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Diff pattern — keep the previous position_tickets and compare to spot new / closed positions.
  • Cheap — only integers cross the wire; use it as a change detector, then pull detail with opened_orders when the set changes.
  • Returns a Subscription — sub.cancel to stop; don't cancel inside the block.

docs.title: 1) Detect opens / closes
docs.text:
prev = []
sub = acct.on_opened_orders_tickets(interval_ms: 1000) do |d|
  now = d.position_tickets.to_a
  (now - prev).each { |t| puts "opened  ##{t}" }
  (prev - now).each { |t| puts "closed  ##{t}" }
  prev = now
end
sleep 20
sub.cancel

docs.title: 2) Live counts
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_opened_orders_tickets do |d|
  puts "positions #{d.position_tickets.size}  pending #{d.pending_order_tickets.size}"
end
sleep 5
sub.cancel

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OpenedOrdersTickets — one-shot combined ticket list.
  • OnOpenedOrdersProfit — P/L on a timer.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#on_tickets.

docs.title: 📡 Streaming Ticks
docs.text:
Stream: live ticks for one or more symbols. Yields OnSymbolMqlTickInfo (bid, ask, time) on a background thread; returns a Subscription.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#on_symbol_tick (aliases subscribe_ticks, subscribe_quotes) (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnSymbolTick (server-streaming)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnSymbolTick(OnSymbolTickRequest) → stream OnSymbolTickReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::SubscriptionService::Stub#on_symbol_tick(request, metadata:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A push stream of ticks — no polling.
  • Why you need it. Live prices for a dashboard, a scalping loop, or a signal engine.
  • Yields OnSymbolMqlTickInfo. The SDK unwraps each reply to reply.data.symbol_tick and calls your block.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Subscribe to ticks for `symbols` (String or Array). Yields OnSymbolMqlTickInfo on a
  # background thread. Returns a Subscription; call .cancel to stop.
  def on_symbol_tick(symbols) { |tick| ... } -> MetaRPC::MT4::Subscription
end

Request message: OnSymbolTickRequest { repeated string symbol_names = 1; }

Reply (stream): OnSymbolTickReply { OnSymbolTickData data; … } — OnSymbolTickData { OnSymbolMqlTickInfo symbol_tick; string terminal_instance_guid_id; }. Your block receives the symbol_tick.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Description symbols Array<String> (or a single String) Symbols to stream. A lone string is wrapped for you. &block block Called with each OnSymbolMqlTickInfo.

docs.title: ⬆️ Yielded — OnSymbolMqlTickInfo
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description symbol symbol String The symbol this tick is for. bid bid Float Best bid. ask ask Float Best ask. last last Float Last price (often 0 on FX). volume volume Integer Tick volume. time time Timestamp Tick time (broker time zone). time_utc time_utc Timestamp Tick time (UTC). time_msc time_msc Integer Tick time in ms (broker). time_msc_utc time_msc_utc Integer Tick time in ms (UTC).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Returns a Subscription — keep it and call sub.cancel to stop. See the Subscription contract.
  • Don't cancel inside the block — deadlocks. Cancel from the main thread.
  • Blocking convenience — MT4Service#each_tick(symbols, seconds:) subscribes, pumps for N seconds, and cancels for you.
  • No auto-reconnect — on a drop, sub.error is set; resubscribe yourself.

docs.title: 1) Run for 5 seconds
docs.text:
got = 0
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") do |tick|
  got += 1
  puts "#{tick.symbol} #{tick.bid}/#{tick.ask}"
end
sleep 5
sub.cancel
puts "received #{got} (#{sub.count} total)"

docs.title: 2) Several symbols
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]) { |t| puts "#{t.symbol} #{t.bid}" }
sleep 3
sub.cancel

docs.title: 3) Cancel from the main thread on a condition
docs.text:
done = false
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") { |t| done = true if t.bid >= 1.1000 }
sleep 0.1 until done || !sub.alive?
sub.cancel

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• Quote — one-shot price (poll).
  • OnTrade — order events.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#subscribe_ticks / #each_tick.

Back to: Streaming Methods — Overview · MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: 🔔 Streaming Trade Events
docs.text:
Stream: fires whenever orders open, update, or close. Yields OnTradeData (new / updated / removed orders + a live account snapshot) on a background thread.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account#on_trade (from the metarpc_mt4 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnTrade (server-streaming)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnTrade(OnTradeRequest) → stream OnTradeReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt4TermApi::SubscriptionService::Stub#on_trade(request, metadata:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A push stream of trade-book changes — you learn immediately when something fills, is modified, or closes.
  • Why you need it. Keep a local order cache in sync; trigger follow-up logic on fills; audit activity.
  • Yields OnTradeData. The SDK calls your block with each event payload.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Account
  # Subscribe to trade events. Yields OnTradeData on a background thread.
  # Returns a Subscription; call .cancel to stop.
  def on_trade { |event| ... } -> MetaRPC::MT4::Subscription
end

Request message: OnTradeRequest {} (empty)

Reply (stream): OnTradeReply { OnTradeData data; … }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Argument Type Description &block block Called with each OnTradeData.

docs.title: ⬆️ Yielded — OnTradeData
docs.text: Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description type type Symbol Event group — MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE (:OrderProfit / :OrderUpdate). event_data event_data OnTadeEventData The order deltas (see below). account_info account_info OnEventAccountInfo Live account snapshot (balance, equity, margin, free_margin, profit, margin_level, login). terminal_instance_guid_id terminal_instance_guid_id String Terminal session id.

docs.title: event_data — OnTadeEventData
docs.text:
Field Type Description new_orders [OnTradeOrderInfo] Orders that just appeared (opened / placed). updated_orders [OnTradeUpdatedOrderInfo] Orders whose SL/TP/price changed. removed_orders [OnTradeOrderInfo] Orders that closed / were deleted. new_history_orders [OnTradeOrderInfo] Newly archived history orders.

The proto message name is OnTadeEventData (a server-side spelling — kept as-is).

docs.title: MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE (on type)
docs.text:
enum MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE {
  OrderProfit = 0;  // a periodic profit update
  OrderUpdate = 1;  // an order opened / modified / closed
}

docs.title: SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE (on the order rows inside event_data)
docs.text:
enum SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE {
  SUB_OP_BUY       = 0;
  SUB_OP_SELL      = 1;
  SUB_OP_BUYLIMIT  = 2;
  SUB_OP_SELLLIMIT = 3;
  SUB_OP_BUYSTOP   = 4;
  SUB_OP_SELLSTOP  = 5;
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Quiet until something happens. No trades → no events; it's not a heartbeat.
  • account_info rides along — each event carries a fresh balance/equity snapshot, handy for a live P/L panel.
  • Returns a Subscription — sub.cancel to stop; don't cancel inside the block.
  • No auto-reconnect — resubscribe on sub.error.

docs.title: 1) Log opens and closes
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_trade do |e|
  e.event_data.new_orders.each     { |o| puts "opened  ##{o.ticket}" }
  e.event_data.removed_orders.each { |o| puts "closed  ##{o.ticket}" }
end
sleep 30
sub.cancel

docs.title: 2) Live equity from events
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_trade { |e| puts "equity #{e.account_info.equity.round(2)}" }
sleep 10
sub.cancel

docs.title: 3) Count events in a window
docs.text:
n = 0
sub = acct.on_trade { |_e| n += 1 }
sleep 5
sub.cancel
puts "trade events: #{n}"

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OnOpenedOrdersProfit — floating P/L on a timer.
  • OpenedOrders — the current book (poll).
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#on_trade.

docs.title: MT4Account · Streaming Methods — Overview
docs.text:
Real-time server streams: ticks, trade events, open-orders profit, ticket snapshots, and connect-state. Each returns a Subscription handle; the SDK reads the stream on a background thread and calls your block for every payload.

Ticks / trades / profit / tickets live on mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService; connect-state on mt4_term_api.Connection. Each method yields its *Data payload to your block.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• OnSymbolTick — live ticks for one or more symbols (OnSymbolMqlTickInfo: bid, ask, time).
  • OnTrade — trade events when orders open / update / close (OnTradeData: new / updated / removed orders + account info).
  • OnOpenedOrdersProfit — open orders' floating P/L pushed on a timer (OnOpenedOrdersProfitData).
  • OnOpenedOrdersTickets — open ticket snapshots (positions + pendings) on a timer.
  • OnConnectState — the terminal's connection state changes (ConnectStateData).

docs.title: 🧵 The Subscription contract
docs.text:
Every streaming method returns a MetaRPC::MT4::Subscription:

sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") { |tick| puts "#{tick.bid}/#{tick.ask}" }
# … your program keeps running; the block fires on a background thread …
sub.cancel          # stop cleanly and wait (up to 5 s) for the reader thread
Method What it does sub.cancel Cancel the stream and join the reader thread. sub.join(limit = nil) Block until the stream ends on its own (or limit seconds). sub.alive? Is the reader thread still running? sub.count How many payloads have been delivered. sub.error The exception that ended the stream, if any (not a clean GRPC::Cancelled).

⚠️ Never call sub.cancel from inside the yielded block — it would deadlock on its own reader thread. Set a flag and cancel from the main thread (or use a blocking helper like MT4Service#each_tick).

No auto-reconnect. If the stream drops, sub.error is set and the block stops — resubscribe yourself. Streams are exempt from the per-call timeout (they are long-lived).

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Yields Live prices (event-driven) on_symbol_tick OnSymbolMqlTickInfo React when orders open/close on_trade OnTradeData Live floating P/L of open orders on_opened_orders_profit OnOpenedOrdersProfitData Detect open/closed tickets cheaply on_opened_orders_tickets OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData Watch the terminal's link health on_connect_state ConnectStateData

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal pattern — run for N seconds
docs.text:
got = 0
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") { |_t| got += 1 }
sleep 5
sub.cancel
puts "received #{got} ticks (#{sub.count} total)"

Or the blocking convenience on the mid layer:

n = sugar.service.each_tick("EURUSD", seconds: 5) { |t| puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}" }

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Poll instead of stream: Quote · OpenedOrdersTickets.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service#subscribe_ticks / #on_trade / #each_tick.
  • Guide: gRPC Streaming.

Back to: MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: MT4Service — Account & Stats (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
9 methods for reading account state and performance — a typed snapshot, the raw summary, demo check, terminal list, server time zone, and the four trade-statistics reads.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a friendly facade over MT4Account that returns a typed Account Struct and passes the stats through.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_service.rb, wrapping account_summary / accounts / server_timezone / trade_stats* / equity_history / trade_unrealized_pl on MT4Account.

Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.rb, sugar/09_sugar_history.rb.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 📋 All 9 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Low-level equivalent account_info Account (Struct) account_summary, composed account_summary AccountSummaryData account_summary (raw passthrough) demo? Boolean account_summary.account_trade_mode == :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO accounts(include_stopped:, page_size:) Array accounts (terminal list) server_timezone ServerTimezoneData server_timezone trade_stats(from_utc:, from:) StatsData trade_stats trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc:, from:, exclude_same_bars:) StatsWithChartsData trade_stats_equity_history equity_history(from_utc:, from:, exclude_same_bars:) [EquityPointData] equity_history trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc:, from:) [TradeUnrealizedExtremaData] trade_unrealized_pl

docs.title: 📦 Account (Struct)
docs.text:
Returned by account_info:

Field Type Description login Integer Account number. balance Float Balance (without floating P&L). equity Float Equity (balance + credit + floating P&L). currency String Deposit currency. leverage Integer Leverage (100 = 1:100). trade_mode Symbol :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO / _CONTEST / _REAL. company String Broker name. server_time_utc Timestamp Broker server time in UTC (read .seconds).

docs.title: account_info -> Account
docs.text:
The account as one typed Struct.

Usage examples:

  1. One-line status: 
    a = service.account_info
puts "##{a.login} on #{a.company} · #{a.balance} #{a.currency} · 1:#{a.leverage}"
  2. Floating P&L (MT4: equity − balance − credit): 
    s = service.account_summary
puts "floating: #{(s.account_equity - s.account_balance - s.account_credit).round(2)}"
  3. Guard before a run: 
    abort "empty account" if service.account_info.balance <= 0

docs.title: account_summary -> AccountSummaryData
docs.text:
The full raw summary (every field, including all margin fields) when the Struct isn't enough.

Usage examples:

  1. Margin picture: 
    s = service.account_summary
puts "used #{s.account_margin}  free #{s.account_margin_free}  level #{s.account_margin_level}%"
  2. Terminal / trade flags: 
    s = service.account_summary
puts "trade allowed? #{s.account_trade_allowed}  EA allowed? #{s.account_trade_expert}"
  3. Credit & investor mode: 
    s = service.account_summary
puts "credit #{s.account_credit}  investor? #{s.is_investor}"

docs.title: demo? -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Refuse to trade on a real account: 
    abort "refusing to trade on a REAL account" unless service.demo?
  2. Branch behaviour by mode: 
    volume = service.demo? ? 0.10 : 0.01
  3. Log the mode once at startup: 
    puts "mode: #{service.demo? ? 'DEMO' : 'LIVE'}"

docs.title: accounts(include_stopped: false, page_size: 200) -> Array
docs.text:
The terminals owned by this API key (auto-paged).

Usage examples:

  1. How many terminals: 
    puts "terminals on this key: #{service.accounts.size}"
  2. Include stopped ones: 
    all = service.accounts(include_stopped: true)
puts "including stopped: #{all.size}"
  3. List their ids: 
    service.accounts.each { |t| puts t.id rescue nil }

docs.title: server_timezone -> ServerTimezoneData
docs.text:
The broker's UTC offset, for converting *_utc timestamps.

Usage examples:

  1. Print the offset: 
    tz = service.server_timezone
puts "#{tz.server}: offset #{tz.utc_offset_seconds}s (#{tz.source})"
  2. Offset in hours: 
    h = service.server_timezone.utc_offset_seconds / 3600.0
puts "UTC#{h >= 0 ? '+' : ''}#{h}"
  3. Is the value fresh? 
    puts service.server_timezone.source == :SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LIVE ? "live" : "cached"

docs.title: trade_stats(from_utc: nil, from: nil) -> StatsData
docs.text:
Aggregate statistics since a start time (pass from_utc or from; omit for full history).

Usage examples:

  1. Headline numbers: 
    st = service.trade_stats(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
puts "trades #{st.trades}  PF #{st.profit_factor.round(2)}  total #{st.summary.total_profit.round(2)}"
  2. Win/loss split: 
    p = service.trade_stats.profitability
puts "won #{p.won_trades_percent.round(1)}% / lost #{p.lost_trades_percent.round(1)}%"
  3. Drawdown guard: 
    st = service.trade_stats
warn "deep drawdown!" if st.max_equity_drawdown_relative > 0.3

docs.title: trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc: nil, from: nil, exclude_same_bars: false) -> StatsWithChartsData
docs.text:
Stats plus the equity/balance chart in one call.

Usage examples:

  1. Numbers + curve: 
    d = service.trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600, exclude_same_bars: true)
puts "trades #{d.stats.trades}  chart points #{d.charts.size}"
  2. Still-open trades at window end: 
    puts "open at end: #{service.trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).open_trades.size}"
  3. Trade series size: 
    puts service.trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).trades.size

docs.title: equity_history(from_utc: nil, from: nil, exclude_same_bars: false) -> [EquityPointData]
docs.text:
Just the equity-curve points.

Usage examples:

  1. Count & last equity: 
    pts = service.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
puts "#{pts.size} points, last equity #{pts.last&.equity}"
  2. Worst drawdown on the curve: 
    worst = service.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600).map(&:equity_drawdown_relative).max || 0.0
puts "#{(worst * 100).round(1)}%"
  3. Export rows: 
    service.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).each { |p| puts [p.balance, p.equity].inspect }

docs.title: trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: nil, from: nil) -> [TradeUnrealizedExtremaData]
docs.text:
Per-order max/min unrealized P/L (MFE/MAE).

Usage examples:

  1. List extrema: 
    service.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).each do |x|
  puts "##{x.ticket} #{x.symbol}: MFE +#{x.max_unrealized_pl.round(2)} / MAE #{x.min_unrealized_pl.round(2)}"
end
  2. Deepest adverse excursion: 
    worst = service.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600).min_by(&:min_unrealized_pl)
puts "##{worst&.ticket} #{worst&.min_unrealized_pl&.round(2)}" if worst
  3. Count rows: 
    puts service.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).size

Window bounds are strings. The stats methods send from_utc / from as ISO-8601 — the SDK converts a Ruby Time for you. See the low-level pages for the full field tables.

docs.title: MT4Service — Orders & History (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
5 methods for reading orders: the full open book, just the tickets, the positions / pending split done for you, and closed-order history (auto-paged).

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a friendly facade over MT4Account. On MT4 an open market order is the position.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_service.rb, wrapping opened_orders / opened_orders_tickets / orders_history on MT4Account and filtering by order_type in Ruby.

Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.rb, sugar/08_sugar_positions.rb.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 📋 All 5 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Low-level equivalent opened_orders(sort:) [OpenedOrderInfo] opened_orders (raw passthrough) opened_tickets [Integer] opened_orders_tickets positions(magic:, symbol:) [OpenedOrderInfo] opened_orders, filtered to market orders pending_orders(magic:, symbol:) [OpenedOrderInfo] opened_orders, filtered to pending orders order_history(from_utc:, to_utc:, sort:, page_size:) [HistoryOrderInfo] orders_history (auto-paged)

The split. positions keeps only order_type :OO_OP_BUY / :OO_OP_SELL (market = positions); pending_orders keeps the ...LIMIT / ...STOP types (and drops the OO_OP_BALANCE / OO_OP_CREDIT ledger rows). Both accept optional magic: / symbol: filters.

docs.title: opened_orders(sort: :SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC) -> [OpenedOrderInfo]
docs.text:
Every open order (market + pending), raw passthrough.

Usage examples:

  1. List all: 
    service.opened_orders.each { |o| puts "##{o.ticket} #{o.symbol} #{o.order_type} #{o.lots}" }
  2. Newest first: 
    service.opened_orders(sort: :SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC).first(5).each { |o| puts o.ticket }
  3. Total floating P/L across everything: 
    puts service.opened_orders.sum(&:profit).round(2)

docs.title: opened_tickets -> [Integer]
docs.text:
Only the ticket numbers — a cheap poll.

Usage examples:

  1. Print them: 
    puts "open: #{service.opened_tickets.inspect}"
  2. How many are open: 
    puts service.opened_tickets.size
  3. Diff against a previous snapshot: 
    now = service.opened_tickets
(now - prev).each { |t| puts "opened ##{t}" }

docs.title: positions(magic: nil, symbol: nil) -> [OpenedOrderInfo]
docs.text:
Open market orders (= positions), optionally filtered.

  1. All positions: 
    pos = service.positions
puts "open positions: #{pos.size}, floating #{pos.sum(&:profit).round(2)}"
  2. By strategy (magic): 
    service.positions(magic: 600_101).each { |o| puts "##{o.ticket} #{o.profit.round(2)}" }
  3. By symbol: 
    puts "EURUSD positions: #{service.positions(symbol: 'EURUSD').size}"

docs.title: pending_orders(magic: nil, symbol: nil) -> [OpenedOrderInfo]
docs.text:
The working pending orders, optionally filtered.

Usage examples:

  1. All pendings for a symbol: 
    service.pending_orders(symbol: "EURUSD").each { |o| puts "##{o.ticket} #{o.order_type} @ #{o.open_price}" }
  2. By strategy (magic): 
    puts "pending for 130013: #{service.pending_orders(magic: 130_013).size}"
  3. Count all pendings: 
    puts service.pending_orders.size

docs.title: order_history(from_utc:, to_utc: Time.now.utc, sort: :HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC, page_size: 1000) -> [HistoryOrderInfo]
docs.text:
Closed / deleted orders in a window, auto-paged.

  1. Last 7 days, net P/L: 
    h = service.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
puts "closed #{h.size}, net #{h.sum(&:profit).round(2)}"
  2. Newest first: 
    service.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400, sort: :HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC)
       .first(5).each { |o| puts "##{o.ticket} #{o.profit.round(2)}" }
  3. Per-symbol: 
    service.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
       .group_by(&:symbol).each { |s, r| puts "#{s}: #{r.sum(&:profit).round(2)}" }

docs.title: 📦 Quote (Struct)
docs.text:
Returned by quote / quote_many:

Field Type Description symbol String The symbol. bid Float Best bid. ask Float Best ask. high Float Session high. low Float Session low. spread Float ask - bid, computed for you. time_utc Timestamp Tick time in UTC.

docs.title: 📦 SymbolSpec (Struct)
docs.text:
Returned by symbol_params / symbol_params_all — the PascalCase SymbolParamsManyInfo normalized to snake_case:

Field Type Description name String Symbol name. digits Integer Price decimals. point Float Point size. contract_size Float Units per lot. volume_min / volume_max / volume_step Float Lot sizing bounds. stops_level / freeze_level Integer Min SL/TP & freeze distance (points). tick_size / tick_value Float Price / money per tick. trade_mode / exe_mode / calc_mode Symbol Trade / execution / margin-calc mode. currency_base / currency_profit / currency_margin String Currencies. swap_long / swap_short Float Swaps. description / path String Human description / Market Watch path. selected Boolean In Market Watch? bid Float Last bid. time_utc Integer Spec time (UTC). raw SymbolParamsManyInfo The original protobuf, for any field not surfaced.

docs.title: quote(symbol) -> Quote
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Bid / ask / spread: 
    q = service.quote("EURUSD")
puts "bid #{q.bid}  ask #{q.ask}  spread #{q.spread.round(5)}"
  2. Session high/low: 
    q = service.quote("EURUSD")
puts "H #{q.high}  L #{q.low}"
  3. Tick time in UTC: 
    puts Time.at(service.quote("EURUSD").time_utc.seconds).utc.iso8601

docs.title: quote_many(symbols) -> [Quote]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Watchlist: 
    service.quote_many(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]).each { |q| puts "#{q.symbol} #{q.bid}/#{q.ask}" }
  2. Index by symbol: 
    by = service.quote_many(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]).to_h { |q| [q.symbol, q] }
puts by["EURUSD"]&.ask
  3. Spread scan: 
    service.quote_many(service.symbols.first(10)).each { |q| puts "#{q.symbol} #{q.spread.round(5)}" }

docs.title: tick(symbol) -> QuoteData
docs.text:
The raw protobuf quote when you want the untouched message.

Usage examples:

  1. Raw bid/ask: 
    t = service.tick("EURUSD")
puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}"
  2. Tick timestamp: 
    puts service.tick("EURUSD").date_time_utc.seconds
  3. Compare raw vs typed: 
    puts service.tick("EURUSD").ask == service.quote("EURUSD").ask

docs.title: symbols -> [String] · symbol_exist?(symbol) -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Count & membership: 
    puts "total #{service.symbols.size}, has EURUSD? #{service.symbol_exist?('EURUSD')}"
  2. Filter a family: 
    puts service.symbols.select { |s| s.include?("USD") }.size
  3. Guard an unknown symbol: 
    abort "no such symbol" unless service.symbol_exist?("EURUSD")

docs.title: select_symbol(symbol, select = true) -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Add to Market Watch: 
    service.select_symbol("XAUUSD")
  2. Ensure a set is watched: 
    %w[EURUSD GBPUSD USDJPY].each { |s| service.select_symbol(s) }
  3. Remove when done: 
    puts service.select_symbol("XAUUSD", false) ? "removed" : "in use"

docs.title: symbol_params(symbol) -> SymbolSpec · symbol_params_all -> [SymbolSpec]
docs.text:
1. One spec: 
    s = service.symbol_params("EURUSD")
puts "digits #{s.digits}  vol #{s.volume_min}–#{s.volume_max} step #{s.volume_step}  contract #{s.contract_size}"
  2. Round a volume: 
    s = service.symbol_params("EURUSD")
vol = ((0.037 / s.volume_step).floor * s.volume_step).clamp(s.volume_min, s.volume_max)
  3. All specs as a lookup: 
    by = service.symbol_params_all.to_h { |s| [s.name, s] }
puts by["XAUUSD"]&.contract_size

docs.title: tick_value_with_size(symbols) -> [SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Read tick value: 
    info = service.tick_value_with_size("EURUSD").first
puts "tick value #{info.TradeTickValue}  contract #{info.TradeContractSize}"
  2. Batch: 
    service.tick_value_with_size(%w[EURUSD XAUUSD]).each { |i| puts "#{i.symbolName} #{i.TradeTickValue}" }
  3. Money per tick for sizing: 
    tv = service.tick_value_with_size("EURUSD").first.TradeTickValue
puts "risk per 200 ticks at 0.1 lot: #{(tv * 200 * 0.1).round(2)}"

docs.title: bars(symbol, timeframe: :M1, from_utc:, to_utc: nil, page_size: 1000) -> [QuoteHistoryBar]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Last day of M5: 
    bars = service.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :M5, from_utc: Time.now.to_i - 86_400)
puts "#{bars.size} bars, last close #{bars.last&.close}"
  2. A fixed window: 
    service.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, from_utc: Time.utc(2026,1,1).to_i, to_utc: Time.utc(2026,1,8).to_i).size
  3. Average H1 range: 
    b = service.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, from_utc: Time.now.to_i - 86_400)
puts (b.sum { |x| x.high - x.low } / [b.size, 1].max).round(5)

docs.title: last_bars(symbol, timeframe: :M1, count: 50) -> [QuoteHistoryBar]
docs.text:
The newest N bars — widens the lookback until enough exist (weekends / holidays).

Usage examples:

  1. Newest 24 H1 closes: 
    service.last_bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, count: 24).each { |b| puts b.close }
  2. Latest close: 
    puts service.last_bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :M5, count: 1).last&.close
  3. Simple SMA(20): 
    c = service.last_bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :M15, count: 20).map(&:close)
puts (c.sum / c.size).round(5)

docs.title: quote_history(symbol, timeframe: :M1, from_utc:, to_utc: Time.now.utc) -> [HistoryQuote]
docs.text:
The legacy bar endpoint (deprecated — prefer bars).

Usage examples:

  1. Last day of H1 (legacy): 
    puts service.quote_history("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).size
  2. Read bar times: 
    service.quote_history("EURUSD", timeframe: :M15, from_utc: Time.now.utc - 3600)
       .each { |b| puts "#{Time.at(b.time_utc.seconds).utc.strftime('%H:%M')} C#{b.close}" }

docs.title: MT4Service — Trading Operations (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
6 methods to trade with plain arguments: send a market/pending order, the buy/sell shortcuts, modify, close/delete, and close-by.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a thin, friendly passthrough to MT4Account's trade RPCs.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_service.rb, wrapping order_send / order_modify / order_close / order_close_by on MT4Account.

Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.rb, sugar/07_sugar_trading.rb.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: ⚠️ MT4 trade contract
docs.text:
• No retcode. order_send returns OrderSendData with a ticket > 0 when filled. A rejection raises MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError — read e.mql_code (130 invalid stops · 132 market closed · 134 no money · 138 requote).
  • Friendly types. type: accepts :buy :sell :buy_limit :sell_limit :buy_stop :sell_stop (mapped to OC_OP_*).
  • Exactly once. A transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal raises TradeOutcomeUnknown — never auto-retried.

docs.title: 📋 All 6 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Low-level equivalent order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, **opts) OrderSendData order_send buy(symbol, volume, **opts) OrderSendData order_send(type: :buy) sell(symbol, volume, **opts) OrderSendData order_send(type: :sell) order_modify(ticket:, **opts) OrderModifyData order_modify order_close(ticket:, lots:, price:, slippage:) OrderCloseDeleteData order_close (close / delete) order_close_by(ticket:, opposite_ticket:) OrderCloseByData order_close_by

order_send options (**opts): price:, stop_loss:, take_profit:, comment:, magic:, slippage:, expiration_utc:. order_modify options: stop_loss:, take_profit:, price:, expiration_utc:.

docs.title: order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, **opts) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
1. Market buy: 
    r = service.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.10, magic: 600_101)
puts "ticket ##{r.ticket} @ #{r.price}"
  2. With SL/TP: 
    q = service.quote("EURUSD")
service.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.10,
                   stop_loss: (q.bid - 0.0020).round(5), take_profit: (q.ask + 0.0020).round(5))
  3. Pending buy-limit: 
    q = service.quote("EURUSD")
service.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy_limit, volume: 0.10, price: (q.bid - 0.0050).round(5))

docs.title: buy(symbol, volume, **opts) · sell(symbol, volume, **opts) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
Positional-symbol market shortcuts.

Usage examples:

  1. Quick buy: 
    r = service.buy("EURUSD", 0.10, comment: "quick")
puts "##{r.ticket}"
  2. Quick sell: 
    service.sell("GBPUSD", 0.05)
  3. With magic + SL: 
    service.buy("EURUSD", 0.10, magic: 600_101, stop_loss: service.quote("EURUSD").bid - 0.0020)

docs.title: order_modify(ticket:, **opts) -> OrderModifyData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Set SL/TP: 
    service.order_modify(ticket: 465_423_938, stop_loss: 1.0800, take_profit: 1.1000)
  2. Move to break-even: 
    o = service.opened_orders.find { |x| x.ticket == 465_423_938 }
service.order_modify(ticket: o.ticket, stop_loss: o.open_price) if o
  3. Re-price a pending: 
    service.order_modify(ticket: 465_424_047, price: 1.0950)

docs.title: order_close(ticket:, lots: nil, price: nil, slippage: 10) -> OrderCloseDeleteData
docs.text:
Close a market order (full / partial) or delete a pending one.

  1. Full close: 
    out = service.order_close(ticket: 465_423_938)
puts "closed (#{out.mode})"            # OCD_MARKET_ORDER
  2. Partial close: 
    service.order_close(ticket: 465_423_938, lots: 0.05)
  3. Delete a pending: 
    service.order_close(ticket: 465_424_047)   # OCD_PENDING_ORDER

docs.title: order_close_by(ticket:, opposite_ticket:) -> OrderCloseByData
docs.text:
Net out two opposite market orders on the same symbol.

Usage examples:

  1. Close a hedge: 
    out = service.order_close_by(ticket: buy_ticket, opposite_ticket: sell_ticket)
puts "closed by @ #{out.close_price}, P/L #{out.profit.round(2)}"
  2. Find the opposite automatically: 
    o = service.positions(symbol: "EURUSD")
b = o.find { |x| x.order_type == :OO_OP_BUY }; s = o.find { |x| x.order_type == :OO_OP_SELL }
service.order_close_by(ticket: b.ticket, opposite_ticket: s.ticket) if b && s
  3. Guard both tickets: 
    begin
  service.order_close_by(ticket: buy_ticket, opposite_ticket: sell_ticket)
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError => e
  warn e.code
end
