docs.title: MT4Service — Streaming Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
6 methods for real-time data: tick / trade / profit / ticket / connect-state streams, plus a blocking each_tick convenience.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — friendly passthroughs to MT4Account's streaming RPCs, each returning a Subscription.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_service.rb, wrapping on_symbol_tick / on_trade / on_opened_orders_profit / on_opened_orders_tickets / on_connect_state on MT4Account.

Demos: examples/demos/service/05_service_streaming.rb.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 🧵 The Subscription contract
docs.text:
Every streaming method (except the blocking each_tick) returns a MetaRPC::MT4::Subscription:

sub = service.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |q| puts "#{q.bid}/#{q.ask}" }
# … runs on a background thread …
sub.cancel      # stop cleanly (also: sub.join, sub.alive?, sub.count, sub.error)

⚠️ Never call sub.cancel from inside the block — it deadlocks on its own reader thread. Use each_tick for a simple timed run, or set a flag and cancel from the main thread. No auto-reconnect: on a drop, sub.error is set.

docs.title: 📋 All 6 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Low-level equivalent subscribe_ticks(symbols, &block) Subscription on_symbol_tick on_trade(&block) Subscription on_trade on_opened_orders_profit(interval_ms:, &block) Subscription on_opened_orders_profit on_tickets(interval_ms:, &block) Subscription on_opened_orders_tickets on_connect_state(terminal_ids = nil, &block) Subscription on_connect_state (defaults to this terminal) each_tick(symbols, seconds:, &block) Integer (tick count) on_symbol_tick + sleep + cancel

docs.title: subscribe_ticks(symbols, &block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Live ticks (yields OnSymbolMqlTickInfo).

Usage examples:

  1. Several symbols for 3 s: 
    sub = service.subscribe_ticks(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]) { |t| puts "#{t.symbol} #{t.bid}" }
sleep 3
sub.cancel
  2. Count ticks: 
    n = 0
sub = service.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |_t| n += 1 }
sleep 2; sub.cancel
puts "#{n} ticks (#{sub.count} total)"

docs.title: on_trade(&block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Fires on order open / update / close (yields OnTradeData).

Usage examples:

  1. Log opens & closes: 
    sub = service.on_trade do |e|
  e.event_data.new_orders.each     { |o| puts "opened ##{o.ticket}" }
  e.event_data.removed_orders.each { |o| puts "closed ##{o.ticket}" }
end
sleep 30
sub.cancel
  2. Live equity from events: 
    sub = service.on_trade { |e| puts "equity #{e.account_info.equity.round(2)}" }
sleep 10; sub.cancel

docs.title: on_opened_orders_profit(interval_ms: 1000, &block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Open orders' floating P/L on a timer (yields OnOpenedOrdersProfitData).

Usage examples:

  1. Live total floating P/L: 
    sub = service.on_opened_orders_profit(interval_ms: 1000) do |d|
  puts "floating #{d.opened_orders_with_profit_updated.sum(&:order_profit).round(2)}"
end
sleep 10
sub.cancel
  2. Per-order rows: 
    sub = service.on_opened_orders_profit do |d|
  d.opened_orders_with_profit_updated.each { |o| puts "##{o.ticket} #{o.order_profit.round(2)}" }
end
sleep 5; sub.cancel

docs.title: on_tickets(interval_ms: 1000, &block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Open ticket snapshots on a timer (yields OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData with position_tickets / pending_order_tickets).

Usage examples:

  1. Live counts: 
    sub = service.on_tickets { |d| puts "pos #{d.position_tickets.size} / pend #{d.pending_order_tickets.size}" }
sleep 5
sub.cancel
  2. Detect opens/closes: 
    prev = []
sub = service.on_tickets do |d|
  now = d.position_tickets.to_a
  (now - prev).each { |t| puts "opened ##{t}" }; prev = now
end
sleep 20; sub.cancel

docs.title: on_connect_state(terminal_ids = nil, &block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Terminal connect-state changes (yields ConnectStateData). Defaults to this client's terminal.

Usage examples:

  1. Watch link health: 
    sub = service.on_connect_state { |st| puts "#{st.state} connected=#{st.is_connected}" }
sleep 5
sub.cancel
  2. Alert on disconnect: 
    sub = service.on_connect_state { |st| warn "down: #{st.error_message}" unless st.is_connected }
sleep 30; sub.cancel

docs.title: each_tick(symbols, seconds:, &block) -> Integer
docs.text:
Blocking convenience: subscribe, pump the block for seconds, cancel cleanly, return the tick count.

Usage examples:

  1. Sample for 5 s: 
    n = service.each_tick("EURUSD", seconds: 5) { |t| puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}" }
puts "#{n} ticks"
  2. Just count, no printing: 
    puts service.each_tick(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD], seconds: 3) { |_t| }

docs.title: MT4Service — Mid-Level API Overview
docs.text:
A convenient wrapper over MT4Account that returns plain Ruby objects (Structs) and plain arguments instead of protobuf messages.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — the balance between low-level (MT4Account) and high-level (MT4Sugar).

docs.title: ⚠️ Same calls, cleaner results
docs.text:
MT4Service and MT4Account make the same gRPC calls — the difference is the return shape, not the logic.

# Low-level (MT4Account) — you read the protobuf quote:
t = account.quote("EURUSD")
spread = t.ask - t.bid

# Mid-level (MT4Service) — you get a tidy Quote struct:
q = service.quote("EURUSD")       # Quote(symbol, bid, ask, high, low, spread, time_utc)
spread = q.spread

What the mid layer does for you

  • ✅ Builds the protobuf *Request from plain arguments.
  • ✅ Returns typed Ruby Structs where they add value — Account, Quote, SymbolSpec.
  • ✅ Auto-pages history reads and hands back ready arrays.
  • ✅ Splits open orders into positions (market) and pending — positions(magic:, symbol:) / pending_orders(...).
  • ✅ Keeps the raw protobuf *Data where the full shape matters (orders, stats) — one hop from the low layer.

Both layers are equally valid — pick the altitude you prefer. For one-liners, go up again to MT4Sugar.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture layers
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  MT4Sugar      one-liners, risk-based sizing│  ← highest
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  MT4Service    plain args → typed structs   │  ← YOU ARE HERE
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  MT4Account    raw protobuf / gRPC          │  ← lowest
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Each layer owns the one below it: MT4Sugar owns an MT4Service, which owns an MT4Account. From here you can always drop down with service.account.

docs.title: 🧱 Construction & lifecycle
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

# Build a fresh MT4Account underneath, or wrap one you already have:
service = MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Service.new(api_key: ENV["MRPC_API_KEY"])
# service = MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Service.new(existing_account)

service.connect(1235959737, "password", server: "EGlobal-Demo")

a = service.account_info            # Account struct
puts "#{a.login}  #{a.balance} #{a.currency}  1:#{a.leverage}"

service.disconnect
  • MT4Service.new(account = nil, **opts) → wraps account, or builds a fresh MT4Account from **opts (api_key:, id:, host, port, timeout:).
  • service.account → the underlying MT4Account (drop down a layer any time).

docs.title: Connection & session helpers (delegated to MT4Account)
docs.text:
Method What it does connect(login, password, server:, **opts) Connect by broker server name (ConnectEx). connect_by_host(login, password, host:, port:, **opts) Connect by raw host:port. connect_proxy(login, password, **opts) Connect through a proxy. get_id(login, password) Resolve the terminal session id (GetId). connected? Local connected flag. check_connect / connect_state / connection_status Health checks. reconnect(force:) Re-establish the broker connection. disconnect(delete:, reason:) Stop the terminal (delete: true removes it). close Release local gRPC channels.

Tuning timeouts. Unary reads use the underlying account.timeout (seconds, default 60); set service.account.timeout = 30 to change it.

docs.title: 📁 Method groups (feature methods)
docs.text: # Group Methods 1 Account & Stats (9) account_info · account_summary · demo? · accounts · server_timezone · trade_stats · trade_stats_equity_history · equity_history · trade_unrealized_pl 2 Orders & History (5) opened_orders · opened_tickets · positions · pending_orders · order_history 3 Symbols & Quotes (12) quote · quote_many · tick · symbols · symbol_exist? · select_symbol · symbol_params · symbol_params_all · tick_value_with_size · bars · last_bars · quote_history 4 Trading Operations (6) order_send · buy · sell · order_modify · order_close · order_close_by 5 Streaming Methods (6) subscribe_ticks · on_trade · on_opened_orders_profit · on_tickets · on_connect_state · each_tick

docs.title: 🧾 The typed objects (Structs)
docs.text:
MT4Service returns three Structs; everything else is the raw protobuf *Data (one hop from MT4Account).

Struct From Fields Account account_info login, balance, equity, currency, leverage, trade_mode, company, server_time_utc Quote quote, quote_many symbol, bid, ask, high, low, spread, time_utc SymbolSpec symbol_params, symbol_params_all name, digits, point, contract_size, volume_min/max/step, stops_level, freeze_level, tick_size, tick_value, trade_mode, exe_mode, calc_mode, currency_base/profit/margin, swap_long/short, description, path, selected, bid, time_utc, raw

Raw protobuf still comes back from: opened_orders / positions / pending_orders (OpenedOrderInfo), order_send (OrderSendData), tick (QuoteData), bars (QuoteHistoryBar[]), the stats methods (StatsData / EquityPointData[]), order_history (HistoryOrderInfo[]).

docs.title: 1) Account snapshot
docs.text:
a = service.account_info
puts "##{a.login} · #{a.balance} #{a.currency} · 1:#{a.leverage}"

docs.title: 2) Current price
docs.text:
q = service.quote("EURUSD")
puts "Bid #{q.bid}, Ask #{q.ask}, Spread #{q.spread.round(5)}"

docs.title: 3) Place an order (MT4: ticket > 0 = filled)
docs.text:
r = service.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, stop_loss: 1.08, take_profit: 1.09)
puts r.ticket.positive? ? "✅ order ##{r.ticket}" : "❌ not filled"

docs.title: 4) Live price + floating P&L
docs.text:
t = service.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |q| puts "tick #{q.bid} #{q.ask}" }
p = service.on_opened_orders_profit { |d| puts "floating: #{d.opened_orders_with_profit_updated.sum(&:order_profit).round(2)}" }
# later: t.cancel; p.cancel

docs.title: 📊 Low-level vs mid-level
docs.text: Aspect MT4Account (low) MT4Service (mid) Arguments plain args, builds *Request plain args Return protobuf *Data Struct (where it helps) or *Data Quotes quote → QuoteData quote → Quote(bid, ask, spread, …) Account account_summary → *Data account_info → Account struct Specs symbol_params_many → PascalCase symbol_params → SymbolSpec (snake_case) Orders one list, filter by order_type positions / pending_orders split for you History manual paging auto-paged arrays Best for every field, full control everyday app code

docs.title: 🔧 Best practices
docs.text:
1. Handle errors with begin/rescue. Every method raises on failure — a server rejection raises MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError (carrying the mql code), a transport failure raises the gRPC error.
begin
  a = service.account_info
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError => e
  warn "failed: #{e.message}"
end

  1. MT4 has no trade retcode. order_send returns OrderSendData with a ticket > 0 when filled; a rejection raises (e.mql_code: 130/132/134…). A transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal is raised as a TradeOutcomeUnknown-marked error — do not blindly retry.

  2. Tune the timeout via service.account.timeout (seconds) for slow links or heavy history pulls.

  3. Always cancel streaming subscriptions when done — they run on a background thread and don't stop on their own.

  4. Free the terminal with service.disconnect(delete: true) at the end of a one-shot run (a trial allows one terminal per IP).

docs.title: 🎯 Summary
docs.text: MT4Service is the everyday layer: the same gRPC calls as MT4Account, but plain arguments in and tidy Ruby objects out — typed Account / Quote / SymbolSpec Structs, auto-paged history, positions split from pendings, no manual request building. Drop to MT4Account for full control, go up to MT4Sugar for one-liners.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Connection (High-Level API)
docs.text:
One-liners to connect, check health, and disconnect — plus the quick_connect positional shorthand.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — delegates to MT4Service / MT4Account.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/main.rb (connects once for every demo).

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 11 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Notes connect(login, password, server:, **opts) ConnectData ConnectEx by broker server name connect_by_host(login, password, host:, port:, **opts) ConnectData by raw host:port connect_proxy(login, password, **opts) ConnectProxyData through a proxy quick_connect(login, password, server) ConnectData positional-server shorthand get_id(login = nil, password = nil) String resolve the session id (GetId) connected? Boolean local connected flag reconnect(force: false) ReconnectData re-establish the broker link disconnect(delete: false, reason: nil) DisconnectData stop the terminal check_connect CheckConnectData health check connect_state ConnectStateData current state connection_status ConnectionStatusData current status

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
These are thin passthroughs to the connection helpers on MT4Account (via MT4Service) — the sugar layer adds friendly names, not new logic:

sugar.connect → service.connect → account.connect → Connection.ConnectEx RPC
  • connect / connect_by_host / connect_proxy → ConnectEx / Connect / ConnectProxy. quick_connect is connect with a positional server.
  • get_id → GetId; reconnect → Reconnect; disconnect → Disconnect.
  • connected? reads a LOCAL flag (no round-trip). check_connect / connect_state / connection_status are the live health-check RPCs.

docs.title: connect(login, password, server:, **opts) -> ConnectData
docs.text:
Connect by broker server name (ConnectEx). Raises InvalidLoginError on bad credentials.

Usage examples:

  1. Basic connect: 
    mt4.connect(1235959737, "password", server: "EGlobal-Demo")
  2. With a stable terminal id (set on create): 
    mt4 = MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Sugar.create(api_key: ENV["MRPC_API_KEY"], id: stable_uuid)
mt4.connect(1235959737, "password", server: "EGlobal-Demo", name: "bot")
  3. Guard bad credentials: 
    begin
  mt4.connect(1235959737, "wrong", server: "EGlobal-Demo")
rescue MetaRPC::MT4::InvalidLoginError => e
  warn "bad login: #{e.message}"
end

docs.title: connect_by_host(login, password, host:, port:, **opts) -> ConnectData
docs.text:
Connect by the broker trade server's raw host:port (Connect).

Usage examples:

  1. Connect by host:port: 
    mt4.connect_by_host(1235959737, "password", host: "1.2.3.4", port: 443)
  2. With a label: 
    mt4.connect_by_host(1235959737, "password", host: "1.2.3.4", port: 443, name: "bot")

docs.title: connect_proxy(login, password, **opts) -> ConnectProxyData
docs.text:
Connect through a SOCKS/HTTP proxy (ConnectProxy).

Usage examples:

  1. Through a SOCKS/HTTP proxy: 
    mt4.connect_proxy(1235959737, "password", host: "1.2.3.4", port: 443,
                  proxy_host: "10.0.0.1", proxy_port: 1080, proxy_type: :PROXY_TYPE_SOCKS5)
  2. With proxy auth: 
    mt4.connect_proxy(1235959737, "password", host: "1.2.3.4", port: 443,
                  proxy_host: "10.0.0.1", proxy_port: 1080, proxy_type: :PROXY_TYPE_HTTP,
                  proxy_user: "u", proxy_password: "p")

docs.title: quick_connect(login, password, server) -> ConnectData
docs.text:
Positional-server shorthand (no server: keyword).

Usage examples:

  1. One line: 
    mt4.quick_connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo")
  2. From env: 
    mt4.quick_connect(ENV["MT4_LOGIN"].to_i, ENV["MT4_PASSWORD"], ENV["MT4_SERVER"])

docs.title: get_id(login = nil, password = nil) -> String
docs.text:
Resolve the terminal session id without connecting.

Usage examples:

  1. Resolve by credentials: 
    puts mt4.get_id(1235959737, "password")
  2. Reuse the cached id after connect: 
    mt4.connect(1235959737, "password", server: "EGlobal-Demo")
puts mt4.account.id

docs.title: connected? -> Boolean
docs.text:
A LOCAL flag set on connect — it does NOT ping the server; use the health checks for a live round-trip.

Usage examples:

  1. Check: 
    puts mt4.connected?
  2. Guard before trading: 
    abort "not connected" unless mt4.connected?

docs.title: reconnect(force: false) -> ReconnectData
docs.text:
Re-establish the broker link with the stored parameters (Reconnect).

Usage examples:

  1. Re-establish: 
    mt4.reconnect
  2. Force it: 
    mt4.reconnect(force: true)

docs.title: disconnect(delete: false, reason: nil) -> DisconnectData
docs.text:
Stop the terminal (Disconnect); delete: true also removes it from the account list.

Usage examples:

  1. Stop (keep the terminal warm): 
    mt4.disconnect
  2. Stop and remove the terminal: 
    mt4.disconnect(delete: true)

docs.title: check_connect · connect_state · connection_status
docs.text:
Health checks (return the raw *Data).

Usage examples:

  1. Is the terminal attached? 
    puts mt4.check_connect
  2. Current state / status: 
    puts mt4.connect_state
puts mt4.connection_status

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Risk Management (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Position-sizing one-liners. ⚠️ MT4 has no server-side margin/profit calc RPC, so these are local estimates from the symbol spec + account leverage — guides, not broker-exact figures.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — computed from symbol_info + account_summary.account_leverage.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/10_sugar_advanced.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 3 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Formula (estimate) required_margin(symbol, volume, price) Float / nil volume × contract_size × price / leverage max_lot(symbol, price) Float free_margin / required_margin(1 lot), floored to volume step pip_value(symbol) Float / nil tick_value × (pip / tick_size)

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
⚠️ MT4 has no OrderCalcMargin / OrderCalcProfit RPC (those are MT5), so these are computed locally from two reads — the symbol spec and the account leverage — never fetched:

sugar.required_margin → symbol_info (SymbolParamsMany) + account_summary.account_leverage
                      → volume × contract_size × price / leverage
  • required_margin and pip_value are formulas over the SymbolSpec; max_lot divides free_margin by the per-lot margin. Treat them as estimates (brokers apply their own margin rules).

docs.title: required_margin(symbol, volume, price) -> Float
docs.text:
ESTIMATED margin to open volume lots at price (leverage-based).

Usage examples:

  1. Estimate for a trade: 
    puts mt4.required_margin("EURUSD", 0.10, mt4.ask("EURUSD")).round(2)
  2. Afford check: 
    need = mt4.required_margin("EURUSD", 0.10, mt4.ask("EURUSD"))
puts mt4.free_margin >= need ? "ok" : "too big"
  3. Per-lot cost: 
    puts mt4.required_margin("EURUSD", 1.0, mt4.ask("EURUSD")).round(2)

docs.title: max_lot(symbol, price) -> Float
docs.text:
Largest lot that fits free margin, floored to the symbol's volume step.

Usage examples:

  1. Biggest affordable lot: 
    puts mt4.max_lot("EURUSD", mt4.ask("EURUSD"))
  2. Size at a fraction of the max: 
    vol = (mt4.max_lot("EURUSD", mt4.ask("EURUSD")) * 0.25).round(2)
  3. Guard a zero: 
    m = mt4.max_lot("EURUSD", mt4.ask("EURUSD"))
abort "one lot exceeds free margin" if m.zero?

docs.title: pip_value(symbol) -> Float
docs.text:
Money value of one pip per 1.0 lot.

Usage examples:

  1. Read it: 
    puts mt4.pip_value("EURUSD")
  2. Money risk of a stop: 
    stop_pips = 20
puts (mt4.pip_value("EURUSD") * stop_pips * 0.10).round(2)   # for 0.10 lot
  3. Lots for a money risk: 
    risk = mt4.balance * 0.01
lots = (risk / (mt4.pip_value("EURUSD") * 20)).round(2)       # 20-pip stop

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Streaming (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Real-time one-liners: tick / trade / profit / ticket / connect-state streams, plus the blocking each_tick.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — passthroughs to MT4Service streams. Each returns a Subscription (except each_tick).

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/lowlevel/03_streaming_methods.rb, service/05_service_streaming.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 🧵 The Subscription contract
docs.text:
sub = mt4.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |t| puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}" }
sub.cancel          # also: sub.join, sub.alive?, sub.count, sub.error

⚠️ Never call sub.cancel inside the block (deadlock). Use each_tick for a timed run, or cancel from the main thread. No auto-reconnect.

docs.title: 📋 All 6 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Yields subscribe_ticks(symbols, &block) Subscription OnSymbolMqlTickInfo on_trade(&block) Subscription OnTradeData on_opened_orders_profit(interval_ms:, &block) Subscription OnOpenedOrdersProfitData on_tickets(interval_ms:, &block) Subscription OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData on_connect_state(terminal_ids = nil, &block) Subscription ConnectStateData each_tick(symbols, seconds:, &block) Integer (blocking; returns tick count)

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
Each streamer forwards 1:1 to an MT4Account streaming RPC and returns a Subscription (a background thread + your block). Ticks/trades/profit/tickets live on SubscriptionService; connect-state on Connection:

sugar.subscribe_ticks → service.subscribe_ticks → account.on_symbol_tick → SubscriptionService.OnSymbolTick
  • on_trade → OnTrade; on_opened_orders_profit → OnOpenedOrdersProfit; on_tickets → OnOpenedOrdersTickets; on_connect_state → Connection.OnConnectState.
  • each_tick is the odd one out — a blocking wrapper that subscribes, pumps for seconds, cancels, and returns the count (no Subscription to manage).

docs.title: subscribe_ticks(symbols, &block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Live ticks → OnSymbolTick. Returns a Subscription.

Usage examples:

  1. Several symbols for 3 s: 
    sub = mt4.subscribe_ticks(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]) { |t| puts "#{t.symbol} #{t.bid}" }
sleep 3; sub.cancel
  2. Count ticks: 
    n = 0
sub = mt4.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |_t| n += 1 }
sleep 2; sub.cancel
puts n

docs.title: on_trade(&block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Order open / modify / close events → OnTrade.

Usage examples:

  1. Log opens & closes: 
    sub = mt4.on_trade do |e|
  e.event_data.new_orders.each     { |o| puts "opened ##{o.ticket}" }
  e.event_data.removed_orders.each { |o| puts "closed ##{o.ticket}" }
end
sleep 30; sub.cancel
  2. Live equity: 
    sub = mt4.on_trade { |e| puts e.account_info.equity.round(2) }
sleep 10; sub.cancel

docs.title: on_opened_orders_profit(interval_ms: 1000, &block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Open orders' P/L on a timer → OnOpenedOrdersProfit.

Usage examples:

  1. Live floating P/L: 
    sub = mt4.on_opened_orders_profit { |d| puts d.opened_orders_with_profit_updated.sum(&:order_profit).round(2) }
sleep 10; sub.cancel
  2. Slower cadence: 
    sub = mt4.on_opened_orders_profit(interval_ms: 3000) { |_d| }
sleep 10; sub.cancel

docs.title: on_tickets(interval_ms: 1000, &block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Open ticket snapshots on a timer → OnOpenedOrdersTickets.

Usage examples:

  1. Live counts: 
    sub = mt4.on_tickets { |d| puts "pos #{d.position_tickets.size} / pend #{d.pending_order_tickets.size}" }
sleep 5; sub.cancel
  2. Detect opens: 
    prev = []
sub = mt4.on_tickets { |d| now = d.position_tickets.to_a; (now - prev).each { |t| puts "opened ##{t}" }; prev = now }
sleep 20; sub.cancel

docs.title: on_connect_state(terminal_ids = nil, &block) -> Subscription
docs.text:
Terminal connect-state changes → Connection.OnConnectState.

Usage examples:

  1. Watch link health: 
    sub = mt4.on_connect_state { |st| puts "#{st.state} connected=#{st.is_connected}" }
sleep 5; sub.cancel
  2. Alert on disconnect: 
    sub = mt4.on_connect_state { |st| warn "down: #{st.error_message}" unless st.is_connected }
sleep 30; sub.cancel

docs.title: each_tick(symbols, seconds:, &block) -> Integer
docs.text:
Blocking: subscribe, pump for seconds, cancel, return the tick count.

Usage examples:

  1. Sample for 5 s: 
    n = mt4.each_tick("EURUSD", seconds: 5) { |t| puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}" }
puts "#{n} ticks"
  2. Just count: 
    puts mt4.each_tick(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD], seconds: 3) { |_t| }

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Money & Account (High-Level API)
docs.text:
One-liners for the money numbers and account snapshot. MT4 has no AccountInfoDouble RPC, so each read comes from one AccountSummary call.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — reads fields off MT4Service#account_summary.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 12 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Source field balance Float account_balance equity Float account_equity margin Float account_margin free_margin Float account_margin_free margin_level Float account_margin_level (percent) credit Float account_credit profit Float equity − balance − credit (floating) account_info Account (Struct) composed account_summary AccountSummaryData raw passthrough demo? Boolean account_trade_mode accounts(**opts) Array terminal list server_timezone ServerTimezoneData broker UTC offset

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
MT4 has no AccountInfoDouble RPC (that's an MT5 feature), so the money one-liners don't each call the server — they all read a field off one AccountSummary read:

sugar.balance → service.account_summary → account.account_summary
              → AccountHelper.AccountSummary RPC → AccountSummaryData.account_balance
  • balance / equity / margin / free_margin / margin_level / credit — a direct field off AccountSummaryData (fetch the summary once, read many fields).
  • profit — computed in Ruby as equity − balance − credit; MT4 has no floating-P/L field.
  • account_info — the same summary, repackaged into a tidy Account struct.
  • demo? — account_summary.account_trade_mode == :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO.
  • accounts / server_timezone — their own small RPCs (Accounts.List / ServerTimezone), not part of the summary.

docs.title: 📖 Method details
docs.text: Each heading below notes what it is and how it's built, then shows usage.

docs.title: balance -> Float
docs.text:
Realized balance (excludes floating P/L). Reads AccountSummaryData.account_balance.

Usage examples:

  1. Print it: 
    puts mt4.balance.round(2)
  2. Empty-account guard: 
    abort "no funds" if mt4.balance <= 0
  3. Risk budget (1% of balance): 
    risk = mt4.balance * 0.01

docs.title: equity -> Float
docs.text:
Balance + credit + floating P/L — the live account value. Reads account_equity.

Usage examples:

  1. Print it: 
    puts mt4.equity.round(2)
  2. Equity-stop trigger: 
    mt4.close_all if mt4.equity < mt4.balance * 0.9
  3. Utilisation vs balance: 
    puts "#{(100 * mt4.equity / mt4.balance).round(1)}%"

docs.title: margin -> Float · free_margin -> Float
docs.text:
Margin locked by open orders, and what's free to open more. Reads account_margin / account_margin_free.

Usage examples:

  1. Used / free: 
    puts "used #{mt4.margin.round(2)}  free #{mt4.free_margin.round(2)}"
  2. Can I afford this trade? 
    need = mt4.required_margin("EURUSD", 0.1, mt4.ask("EURUSD"))
puts mt4.free_margin >= need ? "ok" : "too big"
  3. In market by margin? 
    puts mt4.margin.zero? ? "flat" : "in market"

docs.title: margin_level -> Float
docs.text:
equity / margin × 100, in percent (0 when flat). Reads account_margin_level.

Usage examples:

  1. Percent: 
    puts "#{mt4.margin_level.round(1)}%"
  2. Health gauge: 
    lvl = mt4.margin_level
puts lvl.zero? ? "flat" : (lvl < 200 ? "⚠️ low" : "✅ healthy")
  3. Margin-call watch: 
    warn "near margin call!" if mt4.margin_level.positive? && mt4.margin_level < 120

docs.title: credit -> Float · profit -> Float
docs.text:
credit reads account_credit; profit is computed by sugar as equity − balance − credit (MT4 has no floating-P/L field).

Usage examples:

  1. Floating profit: 
    puts mt4.profit.round(2)
  2. In profit? 
    puts mt4.profit.positive? ? "green" : "red"
  3. Take-profit on the whole book: 
    mt4.close_all if mt4.profit >= 100

docs.title: account_info -> Account
docs.text:
The same AccountSummary read, repackaged into a tidy Account struct (login, balance, equity, currency, leverage, trade_mode, company, server_time_utc).

Usage examples:

  1. Status line: 
    a = mt4.account_info
puts "##{a.login} · #{a.balance} #{a.currency} · 1:#{a.leverage}"
  2. Broker & mode: 
    a = mt4.account_info
puts "#{a.company} (#{a.trade_mode})"

docs.title: account_summary -> AccountSummaryData
docs.text:
The raw protobuf AccountSummaryData — every field — when the Account struct isn't enough. This is the one call the money helpers above all read from.

Usage examples:

  1. Full margin picture: 
    s = mt4.account_summary
puts "used #{s.account_margin}  free #{s.account_margin_free}  level #{s.account_margin_level}%"
  2. Trade flags: 
    s = mt4.account_summary
puts "trade allowed? #{s.account_trade_allowed}  EA? #{s.account_trade_expert}"

docs.title: demo? -> Boolean
docs.text:
True on a demo account — checks account_summary.account_trade_mode == :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO.

Usage examples:

  1. Refuse real: 
    abort "demo only" unless mt4.demo?
  2. Size by mode: 
    vol = mt4.demo? ? 0.10 : 0.01

docs.title: accounts(**opts) -> Array · server_timezone -> ServerTimezoneData
docs.text:
Their own small RPCs (not part of the summary): accounts → Accounts.List (terminals on this key, auto-paged); server_timezone → ServerTimezone (broker UTC offset).

Usage examples:

  1. Terminals on this key: 
    puts mt4.accounts.size
  2. Broker clock offset: 
    tz = mt4.server_timezone
puts "#{tz.server}: #{tz.utc_offset_seconds}s"

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Prices & Quotes (High-Level API)
docs.text:
One-liners for live prices — a single number, or a whole Quote struct.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — wraps MT4Service#quote.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 5 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Description bid(symbol) Float Best bid. ask(symbol) Float Best ask. spread(symbol) Float ask − bid. price(symbol) Quote (Struct) symbol, bid, ask, high, low, spread, time_utc. quotes(symbols) [Quote] Several symbols at once.

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
Prices come from ONE RPC — MarketInfo.Quote (or QuoteMany for a batch). The readers all wrap service.quote, which turns the raw QuoteData into a tidy Quote struct and computes spread for you:

sugar.bid(sym) → service.quote(sym) → account.quote → MarketInfo.Quote → Quote.bid
  • bid / ask / spread / price all read the same Quote struct; spread = ask − bid is computed when the struct is built.
  • quotes(syms) → service.quote_many → MarketInfo.QuoteMany (one call for many symbols).

docs.title: bid(symbol) -> Float · ask(symbol) -> Float
docs.text:
Latest bid / ask — service.quote(sym).bid / .ask.

Usage examples:

  1. Both sides: 
    puts "#{mt4.bid('EURUSD')} / #{mt4.ask('EURUSD')}"
  2. Mid price: 
    mid = (mt4.bid("EURUSD") + mt4.ask("EURUSD")) / 2
  3. Entry reference for a stop: 
    sl = (mt4.bid("EURUSD") - 0.0020).round(5)

docs.title: spread(symbol) -> Float
docs.text:
ask − bid, precomputed on the Quote struct.

Usage examples:

  1. Price units: 
    puts mt4.spread("EURUSD").round(5)
  2. In points: 
    puts (mt4.spread("EURUSD") / mt4.symbol_point("EURUSD")).round
  3. Skip if too wide: 
    next if mt4.spread("EURUSD") > 0.0003

docs.title: price(symbol) -> Quote
docs.text:
The whole Quote struct in one call (symbol, bid, ask, high, low, spread, time_utc).

Usage examples:

  1. Snapshot: 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
puts "bid #{q.bid}  ask #{q.ask}  spread #{q.spread.round(5)}"
  2. Session range: 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
puts "H #{q.high}  L #{q.low}"
  3. Time of the tick: 
    puts Time.at(mt4.price("EURUSD").time_utc.seconds).utc.iso8601

docs.title: quotes(symbols) -> [Quote]
docs.text:
Batched Quotes for several symbols — MarketInfo.QuoteMany in one round-trip.

Usage examples:

  1. Watchlist: 
    mt4.quotes(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]).each { |q| puts "#{q.symbol} #{q.bid}/#{q.ask}" }
  2. Index by symbol: 
    by = mt4.quotes(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]).to_h { |q| [q.symbol, q] }
puts by["EURUSD"]&.spread

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Simple Trading (High-Level API)
docs.text:
One-liners to open orders: market buy/sell and the four pending types. MT4 has no retcode — a filled order returns OrderSendData with ticket > 0.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — wraps MT4Service#order_send.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/07_sugar_trading.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All methods
docs.text:
Method Opens Price arg buy_market(symbol, volume, **kw) (alias buy) market buy — sell_market(symbol, volume, **kw) (alias sell) market sell — buy_limit(symbol, volume, price, **kw) pending buy below required sell_limit(symbol, volume, price, **kw) pending sell above required buy_stop(symbol, volume, price, **kw) pending buy above required sell_stop(symbol, volume, price, **kw) pending sell below required

**kw forwards to order_send: stop_loss:, take_profit:, comment:, magic:, slippage:, expiration_utc:. All return OrderSendData (ticket > 0 = filled); a rejection raises ApiError.

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
Every opener is the SAME RPC — TradingHelper.OrderSend — with a different order type:

sugar.buy_market(sym, vol) → service.order_send(type: :buy) → account.order_send → TradingHelper.OrderSend
  • The friendly :buy / :sell / :buy_limit / … is mapped to the raw enum :OC_OP_BUY / … inside MT4Account (the ORDER_TYPES table). The raw protobuf field needs :OC_OP_*.
  • Market orders omit price (the gateway fills at the live quote); pending orders (*_limit / *_stop) require it.
  • All return OrderSendData — ticket > 0 = filled (no retcode); a rejection raises ApiError.

docs.title: buy_market(symbol, volume, **kw) · sell_market(symbol, volume, **kw) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
Aliases: buy / sell.

Usage examples:

  1. Market buy: 
    r = mt4.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.10, magic: 600_101)
puts r.ticket.positive? ? "✅ ##{r.ticket}" : "❌"
  2. Market sell with a comment: 
    mt4.sell_market("GBPUSD", 0.05, comment: "fade")
  3. Alias form: 
    mt4.buy("EURUSD", 0.01)

docs.title: buy_limit · sell_limit(symbol, volume, price, **kw) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
Pending LIMIT below/above the market → order_send(type: :buy_limit/:sell_limit, price:).

Usage examples:

  1. Buy-limit below the market (join a dip): 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.buy_limit("EURUSD", 0.10, (q.bid - 0.0050).round(5))
  2. Sell-limit above (fade a rally): 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.sell_limit("EURUSD", 0.10, (q.ask + 0.0050).round(5))
  3. With expiry: 
    mt4.buy_limit("EURUSD", 0.10, 1.0900, expiration_utc: Time.now.utc + 3600)

docs.title: buy_stop · sell_stop(symbol, volume, price, **kw) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
Pending STOP above/below the market → order_send(type: :buy_stop/:sell_stop, price:).

Usage examples:

  1. Buy-stop above (breakout up): 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.buy_stop("EURUSD", 0.10, (q.ask + 0.0050).round(5))
  2. Sell-stop below (breakdown): 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.sell_stop("EURUSD", 0.10, (q.bid - 0.0050).round(5))
  3. Breakout bracket (both sides): 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.buy_stop("EURUSD", 0.10, (q.ask + 0.0050).round(5))
mt4.sell_stop("EURUSD", 0.10, (q.bid - 0.0050).round(5))

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Trading with SL/TP (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Open with protective stops in one call, plus the raw order_send / order_modify / order_close passthroughs for full control.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — wraps MT4Service trade methods.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/07_sugar_trading.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 5 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Description buy_market_with_sl_tp(symbol, volume, sl:, tp:, **kw) OrderSendData market buy + SL/TP in one call sell_market_with_sl_tp(symbol, volume, sl:, tp:, **kw) OrderSendData market sell + SL/TP order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, **opts) OrderSendData full-control passthrough order_modify(ticket:, **opts) OrderModifyData change SL/TP/price/expiration order_close(ticket:, **opts) OrderCloseDeleteData close / delete by ticket

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
The SL/TP openers are just order_send with the stop fields filled; the raw passthroughs forward 1:1 to the trade RPCs:

sugar.buy_market_with_sl_tp → service.order_send(type: :buy, stop_loss:, take_profit:) → TradingHelper.OrderSend
sugar.order_modify          → service.order_modify  → TradingHelper.OrderModify
sugar.order_close           → service.order_close   → TradingHelper.OrderCloseDelete
  • No extra RPC for SL/TP — the same OrderSend carries the stoploss / takeprofit fields.
  • order_send / order_modify / order_close are escape hatches for full control (any type: / option).

docs.title: buy_market_with_sl_tp(symbol, volume, sl:, tp:, **kw) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
Market buy + protective SL/TP in one OrderSend.

Usage examples:

  1. Buy with fixed SL/TP: 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.buy_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.10, sl: (q.bid - 0.0020).round(5), tp: (q.ask + 0.0020).round(5))
  2. Risk/reward by pips: 
    pip = mt4.symbol_point("EURUSD") * 10
q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.buy_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.10, sl: (q.bid - 20 * pip).round(5), tp: (q.ask + 40 * pip).round(5))
  3. With magic: 
    mt4.buy_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.10, sl: 1.08, tp: 1.10, magic: 700_008)

docs.title: sell_market_with_sl_tp(symbol, volume, sl:, tp:, **kw) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
The sell mirror of the above.

Usage examples:

  1. Sell with SL above / TP below: 
    q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.sell_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.10, sl: (q.ask + 0.0020).round(5), tp: (q.bid - 0.0020).round(5))
  2. By pips: 
    pip = mt4.symbol_point("EURUSD") * 10
q = mt4.price("EURUSD")
mt4.sell_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.10, sl: (q.ask + 20 * pip).round(5), tp: (q.bid - 40 * pip).round(5))

docs.title: order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, **opts) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
Full-control passthrough (any type: / option).

Usage examples:

  1. Pending with everything: 
    mt4.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy_stop, volume: 0.1, price: 1.10,
               stop_loss: 1.095, take_profit: 1.11, magic: 42, comment: "brk")
  2. Market with slippage: 
    mt4.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, slippage: 5)

docs.title: order_modify(ticket:, **opts) -> OrderModifyData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Set SL/TP:

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Order Management (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Close, cancel, net-out and adjust stops — the verbs you reach for after an order is open.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — composes MT4Service close/modify methods.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/07_sugar_trading.rb, orchestrators/11_trailing_stop.rb, orchestrators/13_grid_trader.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 9 methods
docs.text: Method Does close_order(ticket, lots: nil, slippage: 10) close a market order (full / partial) close_all(slippage: 10) close every open market order close_all_by_symbol(symbol, slippage: 10) close all market orders on a symbol cancel_order(ticket) delete a pending order cancel_all_pending delete every pending order close_by(ticket, opposite_ticket) net out two opposite orders modify_sl(ticket, stop_loss) set the stop-loss modify_tp(ticket, take_profit) set the take-profit modify_sl_tp(ticket, stop_loss:, take_profit:) set both

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
Single-ticket actions are one RPC; the "all" / "by-symbol" helpers are Ruby loops over the open-orders list, not a bulk server call:

sugar.close_order(t) → service.order_close(ticket: t) → TradingHelper.OrderCloseDelete
sugar.close_all      → open_orders.map { |o| close_order(o.ticket) }   # a loop of closes
  • close_order / cancel_order → OrderCloseDelete (close a market order / delete a pending). close_by → OrderCloseBy. modify_sl / modify_tp / modify_sl_tp → OrderModify.
  • close_all / close_all_by_symbol / cancel_all_pending iterate the matching orders and close each — N calls; guard each with rescue if a ticket may already be gone.

docs.title: close_order(ticket, lots: nil, slippage: 10) -> OrderCloseDeleteData
docs.text:
Close a market order (full or partial) by ticket → OrderCloseDelete.

Usage examples:

  1. Full close: 
    mt4.close_order(465_423_938)
  2. Partial close: 
    mt4.close_order(465_423_938, lots: 0.05)
  3. Close the newest position on a symbol: 
    o = mt4.open_orders(symbol: "EURUSD").max_by(&:ticket)
mt4.close_order(o.ticket) if o

docs.title: close_all(slippage: 10) -> Array
docs.text:
Loop: close every open market order (one OrderCloseDelete each).

Usage examples:

  1. Flatten everything: 
    mt4.close_all
  2. Equity-stop kill switch: 
    mt4.close_all if mt4.equity < mt4.balance * 0.9
  3. Count what closed: 
    puts "closed #{mt4.close_all.size}"

docs.title: close_all_by_symbol(symbol, slippage: 10) -> Array
docs.text:
Loop: close every market order on one symbol.

Usage examples:

  1. Flatten one symbol: 
    mt4.close_all_by_symbol("EURUSD")
  2. Only if in profit there: 
    mt4.close_all_by_symbol("EURUSD") if mt4.profit_by_symbol("EURUSD") > 0

docs.title: cancel_order(ticket) · cancel_all_pending -> Array
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Delete one pending: 
    mt4.cancel_order(465_424_047)
  2. Delete every pending: 
    mt4.cancel_all_pending
  3. Cancel pendings on a symbol: 
    mt4.pending(symbol: "EURUSD").each { |o| mt4.cancel_order(o.ticket) }

docs.title: close_by(ticket, opposite_ticket) -> OrderCloseByData
docs.text:
Net out two opposite market orders in a single call → OrderCloseBy.

Usage examples:

  1. Net out a buy and a sell: 
    mt4.close_by(buy_ticket, sell_ticket)
  2. Find the opposite automatically: 
    o = mt4.open_orders(symbol: "EURUSD")
b = o.find { |x| x.order_type == :OO_OP_BUY }; s = o.find { |x| x.order_type == :OO_OP_SELL }
mt4.close_by(b.ticket, s.ticket) if b && s

docs.title: modify_sl(ticket, stop_loss) · modify_tp(ticket, take_profit) · modify_sl_tp(ticket, stop_loss:, take_profit:)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Set a stop: 
    mt4.modify_sl(465_423_938, 1.0800)
  2. Set a target: 
    mt4.modify_tp(465_423_938, 1.1000)
  3. Both at once: 
    mt4.modify_sl_tp(465_423_938, stop_loss: 1.0800, take_profit: 1.1000)

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Order Information (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Read-only one-liners over the open book: list, filter, count, and sum. On MT4 an open market order is a position.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — composes MT4Service#positions / #pending_orders / #opened_tickets.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/08_sugar_positions.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 9 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Description open_orders(magic:, symbol:) [OpenedOrderInfo] open market orders (positions) pending(magic:, symbol:) [OpenedOrderInfo] pending orders order(ticket) OpenedOrderInfo / nil one order by ticket orders_by_symbol(symbol) [OpenedOrderInfo] positions on a symbol has_order?(symbol) Boolean any position on a symbol? count_orders Integer number of open positions total_profit Float summed floating P/L profit_by_symbol(symbol) Float floating P/L for a symbol open_tickets [Integer] tickets (open + pending)

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
MT4 returns ONE open-orders list; these helpers wrap that single OpenedOrders RPC and split/count/sum it in Ruby — only open_tickets is its own call:

sugar.open_orders → service.positions → account.opened_orders (AccountHelper.OpenedOrders)
                  → [OpenedOrderInfo] kept to market types (:OO_OP_BUY/:OO_OP_SELL)
  • open_orders / orders_by_symbol = market orders filtered client-side; pending = the *_limit / *_stop types.
  • count_orders / has_order? / total_profit / profit_by_symbol are pure Ruby over that list (no extra RPC).
  • open_tickets → service.opened_tickets → AccountHelper.OpenedOrdersTickets (just the ids, cheap).

docs.title: open_orders(magic: nil, symbol: nil) -> [OpenedOrderInfo]
docs.text:
Open MARKET orders (= positions), filtered by magic/symbol in Ruby.

Usage examples:

  1. List positions: 
    mt4.open_orders.each { |o| puts "##{o.ticket} #{o.symbol} #{o.lots} #{o.profit.round(2)}" }
  2. By strategy: 
    puts mt4.open_orders(magic: 600_101).size
  3. By symbol: 
    puts mt4.open_orders(symbol: "EURUSD").size

docs.title: pending(magic: nil, symbol: nil) -> [OpenedOrderInfo]
docs.text:
The working pending orders (the *_limit / *_stop types).

Usage examples:

  1. All pendings: 
    mt4.pending.each { |o| puts "##{o.ticket} #{o.order_type} @ #{o.open_price}" }
  2. Pendings on a symbol: 
    puts mt4.pending(symbol: "EURUSD").size

docs.title: order(ticket) -> OpenedOrderInfo / nil
docs.text:
One open order by ticket (market or pending) — opened_orders.find.

Usage examples:

  1. Look one up: 
    o = mt4.order(465_423_938)
puts o ? "#{o.symbol} #{o.lots}" : "gone"
  2. Read its SL/TP: 
    o = mt4.order(465_423_938)
puts "SL #{o&.stop_loss}  TP #{o&.take_profit}"

docs.title: orders_by_symbol(symbol) · has_order?(symbol) · count_orders
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Positions on a symbol: 
    puts mt4.orders_by_symbol("EURUSD").size
  2. Any open there? 
    puts mt4.has_order?("EURUSD")
  3. Total open positions: 
    puts mt4.count_orders

docs.title: total_profit · profit_by_symbol(symbol)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Whole-book floating P/L: 
    puts mt4.total_profit.round(2)
  2. For one symbol: 
    puts mt4.profit_by_symbol("EURUSD").round(2)
  3. Take-profit rule: 
    mt4.close_all_by_symbol("EURUSD") if mt4.profit_by_symbol("EURUSD") >= 50

docs.text:
Just the open tickets — its own lightweight OpenedOrdersTickets RPC.

Usage examples:

  1. All tickets: 
    puts mt4.open_tickets.inspect
  2. Count: 
    puts mt4.open_tickets.size

docs.title: MT4Sugar — History & Statistics (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Closed-order history and the four trade-statistics reads, as one-liners.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — passthroughs to MT4Service history/stats methods.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/09_sugar_history.rb.

← MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 5 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Description order_history(from_utc:, **opts) [HistoryOrderInfo] closed / deleted orders (auto-paged) trade_stats(from_utc:, from:) StatsData aggregate statistics trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc:, from:, exclude_same_bars:) StatsWithChartsData stats + equity chart equity_history(from_utc:, from:, exclude_same_bars:) [EquityPointData] equity-curve points trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc:, from:) [TradeUnrealizedExtremaData] per-order MFE/MAE

Stats take a start time as from_utc (UTC) or from (broker time), sent as ISO-8601 strings; omit for full history.

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
Two different services: order_history comes from AccountHelper.OrdersHistory (auto-paged), the stats from the separate TradeStats service (the server aggregates):

sugar.order_history → account.orders_history → AccountHelper.OrdersHistory (paged → one array)
sugar.trade_stats   → account.trade_stats   → TradeStats.TradeStats
  • History window bounds are Timestamps; stats window bounds are ISO-8601 strings (the SDK converts a Ruby Time for you) — an MT4-specific split.
  • trade_stats / trade_stats_equity_history / equity_history / trade_unrealized_pl all live on the TradeStats service.

docs.title: order_history(from_utc:, **opts) -> [HistoryOrderInfo]
docs.text:
Closed / deleted orders in a window — auto-paged into one array (OrdersHistory).

Usage examples:

  1. Last 7 days, net P/L: 
    h = mt4.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
puts "closed #{h.size}, net #{h.sum(&:profit).round(2)}"
  2. Newest first: 
    mt4.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400, sort: :HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC)
   .first(5).each { |o| puts o.ticket }
  3. Per-symbol: 
    mt4.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
   .group_by(&:symbol).each { |s, r| puts "#{s}: #{r.sum(&:profit).round(2)}" }

docs.title: trade_stats(from_utc: nil, from: nil) -> StatsData
docs.text:
Server-aggregated stats (TradeStats.TradeStats); from_utc is sent as an ISO-8601 string.

Usage examples:

  1. Headline numbers: 
    st = mt4.trade_stats(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
puts "trades #{st.trades}  PF #{st.profit_factor.round(2)}"
  2. Win rate: 
    puts "#{mt4.trade_stats.profitability.won_trades_percent.round(1)}%"
  3. Growth over the window: 
    puts "#{mt4.trade_stats(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 90 * 24 * 3600).growth_percent.round(1)}%"

docs.title: trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc: nil, from: nil, exclude_same_bars: false) -> StatsWithChartsData
docs.text:
Stats + the equity/balance chart in one call (TradeStatsEquityHistory).

Usage examples:

  1. Numbers + curve: 
    d = mt4.trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600, exclude_same_bars: true)
puts "trades #{d.stats.trades}  points #{d.charts.size}"
  2. Open at window end: 
    puts mt4.trade_stats_equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).open_trades.size

docs.title: equity_history(from_utc: nil, from: nil, exclude_same_bars: false) -> [EquityPointData]
docs.text:
Just the equity-curve points (EquityHistory).

Usage examples:

  1. Last equity: 
    pts = mt4.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
puts pts.last&.equity
  2. Max drawdown on the curve: 
    puts (mt4.equity_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600).map(&:equity_drawdown_relative).max.to_f * 100).round(1)

docs.title: trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: nil, from: nil) -> [TradeUnrealizedExtremaData]
docs.text:
Per-order max/min unrealized P/L (TradeUnrealizedPL).

Usage examples:

  1. Per-order MFE/MAE: 
    mt4.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 86_400).each do |x|
  puts "##{x.ticket} +#{x.max_unrealized_pl.round(2)} / #{x.min_unrealized_pl.round(2)}"
end
  2. Deepest adverse excursion: 
    w = mt4.trade_unrealized_pl(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600).min_by(&:min_unrealized_pl)
puts "##{w&.ticket} #{w&.min_unrealized_pl&.round(2)}" if w

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt4/mt4_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/10_sugar_advanced.rb.

docs.title: 📋 All 11 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Description symbol_info(symbol) SymbolSpec / nil full spec struct all_symbols [String] every symbol name symbol_available?(symbol) Boolean does it exist? select_symbol(symbol, select = true) Boolean Market Watch toggle symbol_digits(symbol) Integer price decimals symbol_point(symbol) Float point size min_stop_level(symbol) Integer min SL/TP distance (points) bars(symbol, **opts) [QuoteHistoryBar] OHLC bars last_bars(symbol, timeframe:, count:) [QuoteHistoryBar] newest N bars tick_value_with_size(symbols) [SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo] money per tick all_symbol_specs [SymbolSpec] every symbol's spec

docs.title: 🏗️ How these are built
docs.text:
The spec one-liners all read ONE SymbolSpec (from AccountHelper.SymbolParamsMany); the rest map to their own small RPCs:

sugar.symbol_digits(sym) → service.symbol_params(sym) → account.symbol_params_many → SymbolParamsMany → SymbolSpec.digits
  • symbol_info / symbol_digits / symbol_point / min_stop_level / all_symbol_specs come from SymbolParamsMany (the SymbolSpec struct).
  • all_symbols → MarketInfo.Symbols; symbol_available? = all_symbols.include?; select_symbol → MarketInfo.SymbolSelect.
  • bars / last_bars → QuoteHistory.Bars; tick_value_with_size → AccountHelper.TickValueWithSize.

docs.title: symbol_info(symbol) -> SymbolSpec
docs.text:
Full SymbolSpec for a symbol (SymbolParamsMany).

Usage examples:

  1. Key spec fields: 
    s = mt4.symbol_info("EURUSD")
puts "digits #{s.digits}  vol #{s.volume_min}–#{s.volume_max} step #{s.volume_step}"
  2. Currencies: 
    s = mt4.symbol_info("EURUSD")
puts "#{s.currency_base}/#{s.currency_profit} margin #{s.currency_margin}"
  3. Round a volume: 
    s = mt4.symbol_info("EURUSD")
vol = ((0.037 / s.volume_step).floor * s.volume_step).clamp(s.volume_min, s.volume_max)

docs.title: all_symbols · symbol_available?(symbol) · select_symbol(symbol, select = true)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Count & membership: 
    puts "#{mt4.all_symbols.size}, has EURUSD? #{mt4.symbol_available?('EURUSD')}"
  2. Add to Market Watch: 
    mt4.select_symbol("XAUUSD")
  3. Guard an unknown symbol: 
    abort "no such symbol" unless mt4.symbol_available?("EURUSD")

docs.title: symbol_digits(symbol) · symbol_point(symbol) · min_stop_level(symbol)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Digits & point: 
    puts "digits #{mt4.symbol_digits('EURUSD')}  point #{mt4.symbol_point('EURUSD')}"
  2. Pip size: 
    d = mt4.symbol_digits("EURUSD")
pip = mt4.symbol_point("EURUSD") * ((d == 3 || d == 5) ? 10 : 1)
  3. Respect the stops level: 
    puts "min SL/TP distance: #{mt4.min_stop_level('EURUSD')} pts"

docs.title: MT4Sugar — High-Level API Overview
docs.text:
One-line helpers for everyday trading: connect, read balances, quote, buy/sell, manage orders, size risk, stream. The friendliest layer — built on MT4Service, which is built on MT4Account.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — maximum convenience, minimum boilerplate.

docs.title: 🧱 One call builds the whole stack
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt4"

mt4 = MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Sugar.create("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443, api_key: ENV["MRPC_API_KEY"])
mt4.connect(1235959737, "password", server: "EGlobal-Demo")

r = mt4.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.10)
mt4.modify_sl_tp(r.ticket, stop_loss: 1.0850, take_profit: 1.1000)
puts "balance #{mt4.balance.round(2)}"
  • MT4Sugar.create(host = "mt4.mrpc.pro", port = 443, **opts) → builds MT4Sugar → MT4Service → MT4Account (opts: api_key:, id:, timeout:).
  • mt4.service → the mid layer · mt4.account → the low layer. Drop down any time.
  • MetaRPC::MT4::Client aliases MT4Sugar — a drop-in friendly entry point.

docs.title: 🛑 How errors surface
docs.text:
MT4 has no trade retcode. Trading one-liners (buy_market, close_order, …) return the result *Data; a filled order has a ticket > 0:

r = mt4.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.10)
puts r.ticket.positive? ? "✅ ##{r.ticket}" : "❌ not filled"

A rejection raises MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError — read e.mql_code (130 invalid stops · 132 market closed · 134 no money · 138 requote). A transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal raises a TradeOutcomeUnknown-marked error — don't blindly retry a trade. Read helpers (balance, bid, connected?) return plain values.

docs.title: 🧮 Pips on MT4
docs.text:
Pip size = point × (digits == 3 || digits == 5 ? 10 : 1). So on 5-digit EURUSD one pip = 0.0001, on 3-digit JPY pairs one pip = 0.01. Read point / digits with symbol_point / symbol_digits.

Risk helpers are estimates. MT4 has no server-side margin/profit calc RPC, so required_margin / max_lot / pip_value are computed locally from the symbol spec + account leverage — treat them as approximations, not broker-exact figures.

docs.title: Strategies — Master Overview
docs.text: Orchestrators and presets built on MT4Sugar — small, readable strategy demos you can run and adapt.

docs.title: ⚠️ Educational demos only
docs.text: Every orchestrator and preset here is a demonstration template, not a production trading system. They use simple signals, no real risk engine, and fixed parameters. Run them on a demo account. Before anything live: understand the algorithm, backtest, forward-test, and add real risk management.

docs.title: 🧩 What's an orchestrator vs a preset?
docs.text:
• Orchestrator — composes several MT4Sugar one-liners into one full strategy lifecycle (open → manage → close). It runs a single playbook.
  • Preset — the layer above orchestrators: it reads the market and picks which orchestrator fits right now. The "brain" / router.
Preset  ─ reads conditions ─▶  picks an Orchestrator  ─ composes ─▶  MT4Sugar one-liners

docs.title: 📁 Orchestrators
docs.text: # Strategy Idea Trades? 11 Trailing Stop open, then ratchet the stop-loss up behind price, lock in profit ⚠ yes (demo) 13 Grid Trader bracket the market with pending limits + stops, then remove them ⚠ yes (demo) 14 Risk Manager monitor floating drawdown, flatten everything on breach (kill-switch) dry-run by default

docs.title: 📁 Presets
docs.text: # Preset Idea 16 Adaptive Market Mode measure spread + volatility → recommend trailing / grid / risk-manager

docs.title: 🟢 MT4 note — orders, not positions
docs.text: On MT4 an open market order is the position, and there is no retcode: a filled order returns OrderSendData with ticket > 0. These demos therefore use open_orders / close_order (not "positions" / "close_position"), and read r.ticket after a trade. See MT4Sugar — API Overview.

docs.title: 🧩 Anatomy of an orchestrator
docs.text:
Every orchestrator is the same four moving parts, wired from MT4Sugar one-liners. Build your own by swapping any one part:

Part The question it answers Sugar you'd reach for 1 · Signal / trigger When do I act? bid / ask / spread, last_bars, a clock 2 · Sizing How big? pip_value, required_margin, max_lot (or a fixed lot) 3 · Entry Place what order? buy_market / buy_limit / buy_stop / *_with_sl_tp 4 · Manage → exit How do I tend & close it? open_orders, modify_sl / modify_sl_tp, close_order / close_all_by_symbol 
signal ─▶ size ─▶ enter (keep the ticket) ─▶ manage in a loop ─▶ exit

The three demos each stress a different part — Trailing Stop = management, Grid = entry geometry, Risk Manager = a pure exit/supervisor loop with no entry. Recombine these parts and you have a new strategy.

docs.title: 🛠️ Building your own scenario — what to consider
docs.text:
A demo is a straight line; a real strategy is a loop that survives surprises. Before you adapt one, think through:

  • Entry conditions — be explicit. What exact read makes you enter? Guard a cold symbol (bid == 0 right after select_symbol) and a wide spread(sym) (skip costly moments).
  • Sizing & risk first, entry second. Decide the money at risk before the order: risk = balance * 0.01, then lots from pip_value and your stop distance. Clamp to volume_min / volume_step and check required_margin <= free_margin.
  • Respect the symbol's rules. SL/TP closer than min_stop_level points are rejected (mql_code 130); round prices to symbol_digits, volume to volume_step.
  • Trades raise — handle it. MT4 has no retcode: a fill is ticket > 0, a rejection raises ApiError (read e.mql_code). Wrap every trade in begin/rescue. On TradeOutcomeUnknown never blindly resend — check open_orders first. See Return Codes.
  • Tag & reconcile. Give every order a magic: number so you can find your orders (open_orders(magic:)) and not touch others'. On a restart, read what's already open before deciding to open more (idempotency).
  • Never loosen a stop. A trailing ratchet only moves SL in your favour. Re-sending an identical SL/TP is also refused (mql_code 1) — only modify when the value actually changes.
  • Timing & the event loop. A sleep loop is fine for a demo; for live, drive off a stream (subscribe_ticks / on_opened_orders_profit) and remember there is no auto-reconnect — watch sub.error and resubscribe.
  • Cleanup. Cancel subscriptions in an ensure; decide whether a crash should leave orders open (a supervisor will close them) or flat.

docs.title: 🔗 Combining orchestrators & presets
docs.text:
Real systems compose these pieces. The patterns that matter:

  • Preset as a router (what the Adaptive demo shows) — one place reads the market and chooses which orchestrator runs now: trend → trailing, range → grid, illiquid → stand down. Re-evaluate on a schedule; don't flip strategies every tick.
  • Risk Manager as a supervisor, not a strategy — it has no entry. Run it alongside any orchestrator (its own thread / loop); it watches drawdown and close_all on breach, overriding everything else. The one you always keep on in production.
  • Isolate by magic + symbol — two strategies on the same symbol will fight over the same open_orders. Give each its own magic number (and ideally its own symbol); filter every read/close by magic: so a strategy only ever touches its own orders.
  • Layer, don't nest blindly — an entry orchestrator opens, a management one (trailing) tends, a supervisor (risk manager) caps the downside. Each acts on a clear slice of the book.
  • One connection, or one per worker — a single mt4 multiplexes reads fine; for several strategies trading hard in parallel, give each its own connection with a stable id: (see Sync vs Async).

A minimal "real" shape — a supervisor always on, a preset choosing the playbook:

mt4 = MetaRPC::MT4::MT4Sugar.create("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443, api_key: ENV["MRPC_API_KEY"])
mt4.connect(ENV["MT4_LOGIN"].to_i, ENV["MT4_PASSWORD"], server: ENV["MT4_SERVER"])

# 1) Supervisor in the background — ALWAYS on, overrides everything
Thread.new do
  loop do
    mt4.close_all if mt4.profit <= -(mt4.balance * 0.10)   # 10% floating-loss kill-switch
    sleep 2
  rescue MetaRPC::MT4::ApiError => e
    warn "supervisor: #{e.code}"
  end
end

# 2) A preset picks the playbook; the chosen orchestrator runs its open→manage→close loop,
#    tagging its orders with a magic number so it only touches its own.
mode = choose_mode(mt4, "EURUSD")       # your router — see the Adaptive preset
run_orchestrator(mode, mt4, "EURUSD", magic: 600_101)

Rule of thumb: keep each orchestrator responsible for one job on one slice of the book, let a preset decide which runs, and let a supervisor cap the whole account. That separation is what makes scenarios safe to combine.

docs.text:
All are registered demos — launch from the interactive menu or directly:

ruby examples/demos/main.rb         # menu
ruby examples/demos/main.rb 11      # trailing stop
ruby examples/demos/main.rb 16      # adaptive preset (read-only)

Credentials come from examples/demos/config/config.json or the MT4_* env vars (see Getting Started).

docs.title: 🪜 Grid Trader Orchestrator
docs.text:
Bracket the market with a symmetric grid of pending orders, list them, then remove them. ⚠ Places real (demo) pending orders, then cancels them.

Demo: examples/demos/orchestrators/13_grid_trader.rb · Run: ruby examples/demos/main.rb 13

docs.title: 💡 What it is
docs.text: A grid surrounds the current price with pending orders so you're positioned whichever way the market breaks. This demo shows the mechanics — it places the grid and then removes it (no position management), so you can see how limits and stops bracket the market.

docs.title: 🧠 Strategy logic
docs.text:
At each level i (spaced step_pts apart from the market) it places four pending orders:

Order Where Fires when… buy_limit below the market price dips into it (join the pullback) sell_limit above the market price rallies into it (fade the spike) buy_stop above the market price breaks out up sell_stop below the market price breaks down

Limits face the market (mean-reversion); stops break out with momentum. Whichever zone price enters, an order triggers.

docs.title: 🧱 Composed from (MT4Sugar)
docs.text: Step Methods Place price · buy_limit/sell_limit/buy_stop/sell_stop List pending(symbol:) Remove cancel_order(ticket) (deletes a pending)

docs.title: 🔧 Code walkthrough
docs.text:
levels = 2         # per side
step_pts = 300     # spacing, points
q = sugar.price(sym)

placed = []
(1..levels).each do |i|
  buy_price  = (q.bid - i * step_pts * point).round(digits)   # below
  sell_price = (q.ask + i * step_pts * point).round(digits)   # above
  b  = sugar.buy_limit(sym,  vol, buy_price)
  s  = sugar.sell_limit(sym, vol, sell_price)
  bs = sugar.buy_stop(sym,   vol, sell_price)   # breakout up
  ss = sugar.sell_stop(sym,  vol, buy_price)    # breakout down
  placed.push(b.ticket, s.ticket, bs.ticket, ss.ticket)   # MT4: keep the tickets
end

# remove the grid — cancel_order on a pending ticket deletes it
placed.each { |t| sugar.cancel_order(t) rescue nil }

docs.title: ⚙️ Tunables
docs.text:
Name Meaning levels number of price levels per side step_pts spacing between levels, in points (wider = fewer, farther orders)

Make it real: keep the grid live, watch fills via on_trade, and add take-profit / stop-loss and a close_all_by_symbol exit.

docs.title: 🛠️ Make it your own — and how it combines
docs.text:
Why it's shaped this way. Limits face the market (mean-reversion), stops ride the breakout — the grid is direction-agnostic, which is why it's a good entry engine when you have no directional view. The demo only places & removes the grid so you see the geometry; the money is in how you manage the fills.

What to consider when you adapt it:

  • Spacing vs the symbol. step_pts should scale with volatility and the symbol's min_stop_level / spread — a grid tighter than the spread just churns.
  • Manage the fills. A placed grid is only half a strategy. Watch fills with on_trade, attach SL/TP (or hand them to a trailing stop), and cap exposure (a grid can accumulate open lots fast).
  • Cancel the opposite side. When a breakout fires one side, usually cancel the other pendings (cancel_order) so you're not left with a straddle.
  • Total-exposure guard. Sum open_orders lots and stop adding levels past a limit.

How it combines. Grid is an entry block → feed its fills into the Trailing Stop manager, and always run the Risk Manager above it — an un-supervised grid caught in a trend is how accounts blow up.

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: Places 4 × levels pending orders and deletes them. Demo accounts only. A level may trigger before removal — the demo guards each cancel_order with rescue.

docs.title: 🛡️ Risk Manager Orchestrator
docs.text:
Poll the account, and if the floating drawdown breaches a limit, flatten everything (kill-switch). ✅ Safe by default — dry_run only reports what would happen.

Demo: examples/demos/orchestrators/14_risk_manager.rb · Run: ruby examples/demos/main.rb 14

docs.title: 💡 What it is
docs.text: A kill-switch caps the worst case. Instead of hoping a losing book recovers, it watches the floating loss and, once it reaches a fraction of the balance, closes every open order at once. The demo ships in dry-run mode: it reports the breach but doesn't trade — flip one flag to arm it.

docs.title: 🧠 Strategy logic
docs.text:
Each check computes the floating drawdown as a fraction of balance:

floating = equity − balance − credit        # MT4 floating P/L (sugar.profit)
drawdown = floating < 0 ? -floating / balance : 0

and fires the kill-switch when it crosses the limit:

if drawdown ≥ max_drawdown
  dry_run ? report("would fire") : close_all
  stop

docs.title: 🧱 Composed from (MT4Sugar)
docs.text: Step Methods Monitor balance · equity · profit · count_orders Enforce close_all

docs.title: 🔧 Code walkthrough
docs.text:
dry_run = true          # true = report only, never close
max_drawdown = 0.50     # kill-switch at 50% of balance lost (floating)
checks = 3

checks.times do |i|
  sleep 1
  balance  = sugar.balance
  equity   = sugar.equity
  floating = sugar.profit                       # equity − balance − credit
  dd = balance.zero? ? 0.0 : (floating.negative? ? -floating / balance : 0.0)

  puts "balance #{balance.round(2)}  equity #{equity.round(2)}  drawdown #{(dd * 100).round(1)}%  orders #{sugar.count_orders}"

  if dd >= max_drawdown
    dry_run ? puts("KILL-SWITCH would fire") : sugar.close_all
    break
  end
end

docs.title: ⚙️ Tunables
docs.text:
Name Meaning dry_run true = report only; false = actually flatten on breach max_drawdown drawdown limit as a fraction of balance (0.50 = 50%) checks how many times the demo polls

Make it real: run the loop continuously (or drive it from on_opened_orders_profit), set dry_run = false, and add an alert (email / webhook) when the switch fires.

docs.title: 🛠️ Make it your own — and how it combines
docs.text:
Why it's shaped this way. It has no entry on purpose — it's a supervisor, the one component whose job is to be boring and always right. dry_run defaults true so you can watch it think before it's allowed to trade.

What to consider when you adapt it:

  • What triggers the switch. Floating-drawdown vs balance is one rule; you might add an equity stop, a daily-loss limit, a margin-level floor (margin_level < 150), or a max-open-orders cap.
  • Run it continuously. Replace the fixed checks loop with a real loop (or drive it from on_opened_orders_profit) so it's always watching.
  • Arm it deliberately. Flip dry_run = false only after you trust the thresholds on a demo; add an alert (log / webhook) when it fires.
  • It must win ties. When the supervisor says flat, the entry strategies must not immediately re-open — gate them on a shared "halted" flag.

How it combines. Run it alongside every other orchestrator, on its own thread. It reads the whole account (not one magic), so it overrides all strategies at once — the account-level backstop in the layering model from the Master Overview.

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: Dry-run by default — reads only, never trades. With dry_run = false it will close_all open orders on a breach. Test the armed version on a demo account with tiny orders.

docs.title: 🎯 Trailing Stop Orchestrator
docs.text:
Open an order, then ratchet its stop-loss up behind the price to lock in profit as the market moves your way. ⚠ Places a real (demo) order.

Demo: examples/demos/orchestrators/11_trailing_stop.rb · Run: ruby examples/demos/main.rb 11

docs.title: 💡 What it is
docs.text: A trailing stop is the simplest profit-protection strategy: you enter, and every tick you move the stop-loss to a fixed distance behind the current price — but only upward. If price keeps rising, the stop follows and your locked-in profit grows; if price pulls back into the stop, you're taken out with the gains you'd already secured.

docs.title: 🧠 Strategy logic
docs.text:
On each tick the orchestrator computes a candidate stop:

candidate_sl = bid − trail_pts × point

and applies the ratchet rule — move the stop there only if it's higher than the best stop so far:

if candidate_sl > best_sl    → modify_sl(ticket, candidate_sl)   # tighten
else                          → hold (never loosen)

That one-way ratchet is the whole idea: the stop can only improve, never give back ground.

docs.title: 🧱 Composed from (MT4Sugar)
docs.text: Step Methods Open buy_market · open_orders Trail bid · modify_sl · symbol_point · symbol_digits Close close_order

docs.title: 🔧 Code walkthrough
docs.text:
point  = sugar.symbol_point(sym) || 0.0001
digits = sugar.symbol_digits(sym) || 5
trail_pts = 150      # stop sits this far below bid
steps = 6            # how many ticks to trail for

# 1. OPEN — buy, then grab the order's ticket (MT4: ticket > 0 = filled, no retcode)
res = sugar.buy_market(sym, vol, magic: 110_011)
o   = sugar.open_orders(symbol: sym).max_by(&:ticket)

# 2. TRAIL — ratchet the stop up, never down
best_sl = nil
steps.times do
  sleep 1
  bid  = sugar.bid(sym)
  want = (bid - trail_pts * point).round(digits)
  if best_sl.nil? || want > best_sl
    best_sl = want
    sugar.modify_sl(o.ticket, want)            # tighten only
  end
end

# 3. CLOSE — exit (a real run lets the stop do it)
sugar.close_order(o.ticket)

docs.title: ⚙️ Tunables
docs.text:
Name Meaning trail_pts trail distance in points (smaller = tighter, gets stopped sooner) steps how many ticks the demo trails for

Make it real: replace the fixed steps loop with a subscribe_ticks stream and let the broker's stop close the order (drop the explicit close_order).

docs.title: 🛠️ Make it your own — and how it combines
docs.text:
Why it's shaped this way. The one-way ratchet (want > best_sl) is the strategy — a stop that can loosen isn't a trailing stop, it's a guess. The fixed steps loop exists only so the demo ends; a real trailing stop lives as long as the order does.

What to consider when you adapt it:

  • Trail distance vs noise. Too tight (trail_pts small) and normal wiggle stops you out; too wide and you give profit back. Base it on volatility — a fraction of the recent ATR (last_bars high−low) — not a constant.
  • Only trail in profit. Start trailing once price has moved your way by trail_pts, so the first stop sits at/above break-even — not from entry.
  • Respect min_stop_level. A stop computed too close to the market is rejected (mql_code 130) — clamp the distance.
  • Drive it off ticks. Replace the sleep loop with subscribe_ticks so the stop reacts to every price, and let the broker's SL do the close (drop the explicit close_order).

How it combines. It's a management block — pair it with any entry (a grid fill, a breakout, a signal). Tag the order with a magic: and trail only orders with that magic so it never touches another strategy's trades. Keep a Risk Manager running above it as the account-level backstop.

docs.text: Places one tiny market order and closes it. Demo accounts only. Respect the symbol's min_stop_level — a stop too close to price is rejected (mql_code 130).

docs.title: 🧠 Adaptive Market Mode Preset
docs.text:
Read two cheap market signals — spread and recent volatility — and recommend which orchestrator fits current conditions. ✅ Read-only analysis.

Demo: examples/demos/presets/16_adaptive_preset.rb · Run: ruby examples/demos/main.rb 16

docs.title: 💡 What it is
docs.text: A preset is the router above the orchestrators. Rather than always running one playbook, it looks at the market now and points you at the strategy that suits it: trend-follow when it's moving, harvest the range when it's calm, step back when it's illiquid. This demo prints the recommendation; a real preset would launch that orchestrator.

docs.title: 🧠 Decision logic
docs.text:
Condition Recommend Why spread > 50 pts 14 Risk Manager illiquid / costly — don't enter, just watch risk ATR > 400 pts 11 Trailing Stop high volatility — ride a move with a trailing stop otherwise (calm) 13 Grid Trader range-bound — harvest the range with a pending grid

Volatility is a simple ATR-style proxy: the average high − low of the last 24 H1 candles, in points.

docs.title: 🧱 Composed from (MT4Sugar)
docs.text: Step Methods Signals spread · symbol_point · last_bars Decide plain Ruby if/elsif on the two signals

docs.title: 🔧 Code walkthrough
docs.text:
point = sugar.symbol_point(sym) || 0.0001

# 1. SIGNALS
spread_pts = (sugar.spread(sym) / point).round
bars = sugar.last_bars(sym, timeframe: :H1, count: 24)
ranges = bars.map { |b| (b.high - b.low) / point }
atr_pts = ranges.empty? ? 0 : (ranges.sum / ranges.size).round

# 2. DECIDE
pick =
  if    spread_pts > 50 then "14 Risk manager — spread wide, avoid entries"
  elsif atr_pts   > 400 then "11 Trailing stop — high volatility, ride it"
  else                        "13 Grid trader — calm, harvest the range"
  end
puts "→ #{pick}"

docs.title: ⚙️ Tunables
docs.text:
Name Meaning spread threshold (50) points above which conditions are "too illiquid to enter" ATR threshold (400) points above which volatility is "high enough to trend-follow" H1 lookback (24) how many candles feed the volatility proxy

Make it real: after choosing, actually launch that orchestrator (call its proc), re-evaluate on a schedule, and add more signals (session time, news windows, trend filters).

docs.title: 🛠️ Make it your own — and how it combines
docs.text:
Why it's shaped this way. A preset separates "what are the conditions?" from "what do I do?" — so you can change the playbook without touching the strategies, and vice-versa. The demo only prints the pick; a real preset launches it.

What to consider when you adapt it:

  • Signals are cheap — be generous. Spread + ATR is a start; add a trend read (SMA slope from last_bars), a session / time-of-day filter, and a news / illiquidity guard.
  • Thresholds are symbol-specific. The 50-pt spread / 400-pt ATR fit a major — derive them from the symbol (a fraction of its average range) rather than hard-coding.
  • Add hysteresis. Don't switch on a single reading — require the condition to hold for N checks, or you'll flip-flop between grid and trailing right at the boundary.
  • Launch, then re-evaluate. After picking, actually run that orchestrator's loop; re-run the preset on a schedule (not every tick) to decide whether to switch.

How it combines. The preset sits on top — it chooses which orchestrator opens. Keep the Risk Manager independent below it: the preset chooses offence, the supervisor is always-on defence. See the layering model in the Master Overview.

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: Read-only — it only reads the spread and recent bars and prints a recommendation. It places no orders.
